# CLAUDE CODE PROMPT — APW Client Tracker: GHL Backfill
Paste everything below this line into Claude Code (run from C:\Users\Blossom\Documents\Claude\Claude CoWork\APW Data Hub or with that folder accessible).

---

## CONTEXT (do not re-derive — this is current as of 2026-08-09)

A live Client Tracking Command Center exists in Notion under Company HUB
(page 3b75bb1f-fef4-8196-aa4e-fcf029dc732d). 54 pseudonymized client records
(First name + Last initial) are loaded from Slack booked-call alerts + Fathom
recordings. Stages are set from Fathom evidence. What Notion still lacks is
what only GHL has: per-contact IDs, appointment statuses, payments, DND flags.

Notion data sources (use Notion MCP if connected; else output CSV):
- Clients & Leads (spine): 5614ffa0-e3d0-40cb-ae64-b32ec52e288c
- Communications Log:      09c1e23f-9c55-468f-b4f2-19c7fe011477
- Documents:               725de51f-afb9-49ba-b121-d325dc33acb1
- Follow-Ups:              c2d10928-b069-4ead-befa-ece0e0808111
- Deals & Payments:        0c2059ee-3910-4eb8-8927-d0a44ccaf53d
- Stage History:           0cd9f603-f15a-4fc2-9169-72bc50826bc7

GHL: location "Prismatic" (WFkoNzKa9J9PxhngsLfl). READ-ONLY. No writes to GHL,
ever, without Alan's explicit approval in-session.

Standing rules:
1. Pseudonymization holds: no phone numbers, emails, or credit-report contents
   go into Notion. Name + GHL Contact ID is the matching key.
2. Verified vs derived vs unknown — label each. No guessed stages or values.
3. Cumulative: update rows, never delete; history stays in Notes.
4. Communicate in checklists; before executing, checklist what you'll do.

## TASK CHECKLIST

- [ ] 1. Pull from GHL (read-only), for every contact with any appointment on
        the "Professionals" (W2/Business Owner) or Medical calendars, all time:
        contact_id, name, per-appointment {date, calendar, status
        (showed/no-show/cancelled/rescheduled)}, pipeline stage + change dates,
        payments/invoices {amount, date, product}, DND/opt-out flag.
- [ ] 2. Save raw export to this folder as GHL_BACKFILL_2026-08-XX.csv
        (columns: contact_id, name, appt_date, appt_status, stage,
        payment_amount, payment_date, dnd_flag). Also upload a copy to the
        Drive "APW Data Hub" folder.
- [ ] 3. Match contacts to the Notion records below (name match; flag
        ambiguities instead of guessing).
- [ ] 4. Update Notion Clients & Leads per match: fill "GHL Contact ID" +
        "GHL Link"; correct Stage ONLY where GHL shows a status Notion lacks
        (current stages are Fathom-verified — do not downgrade them);
        set "Last Touch" if GHL shows a later touch.
- [ ] 5. Create Deals & Payments rows for every payment found (relate to
        client). This answers: close #1 identity (onboarded 7/1, value TBD in
        the W25-W29 tracker — Ed C. is the leading candidate) and any
        collections beyond Jill P.'s $15,000 (W28, already logged).
- [ ] 6. Create Stage History rows for GHL stage-change timestamps if the API
        exposes them; skip cleanly if not.
- [ ] 7. Answer the open questions and write findings to
        BACKFILL_FINDINGS_2026-08-XX.md in this folder:
        - Close #1: who, value, product?
        - W29 (Jul 13-18) "committed pending contract review": who?
        - Chris Bowers: 2 bookings (Slack) or 4 (resync)?
        - Rico Rice's contact: still polluted by Allen Sims' 7/21 mis-booking?
        - Medical calendar: any bookings ever? Where did Jose R. (medical
          director email) route?
        - Pradeep B., Jennifer U., Joe S., Bryan (RE dev, ~$1.4M ask, 8/8
          call): their GHL contacts + booking source (they showed on Fathom
          but never hit the Slack alerts channel — why?)
- [ ] 8. Mark the three Follow-Up rows dated 2026-08-10 in Notion as Done with
        Outcome notes.

## NOTION RECORDS TO MATCH (name → current stage)

Closed Won: Matt L. (MLCS, credit in repair) · Todd L. (MLCS co-owner, PG) ·
Jill P. ($15K, W28) · Ed C. ($150K no-doc BLOC path)

Booked Call (no outcome yet): Kesavan R. · Rena S. · Robert S. · Bryon C. ·

Abayomi S. · Sari G.
Verify-real flags: Lynn N. (possible SCIO team) · Jennifer L. (possible
Losch/SCIO test) — check whether real GHL contacts exist before treating as
leads.

## OUTPUT
End with a checklist: what was pulled, what was updated in Notion (counts),
each open question answered or explicitly still open with the exact blocker.

## Gamma
Gamma creates AI-powered presentations, documents, webpages, and social posts. Only include optional parameters when the user explicitly requests or clearly implies them. Gamma has intelligent defaults - when in doubt, omit. When uncertain about user preferences, ask rather than assume. The read_gamma tool can read the content of an existing Gamma when given its file ID. Existing gammas have a type: "template" or "regular". Only templates can be used with generate_from_template; use get_gammas with type="template" to discover valid templates. Non-template IDs are not valid inputs to generate_from_template. If generate_from_template reports that an ID is inaccessible or not a template, find a valid template with get_gammas(type="template"). If the user's intent is to create a new gamma, but not by using an existing template, then use the generate tool. IMPORTANT: The tools provided by this server cannot edit or modify existing gammas. Do not suggest that you can make changes, adjustments, or refinements to a generated gamma. Instead, let the user know they can customize their gamma directly in the Gamma editor.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Krisp
This server provides access to the authenticated user's Krisp workspace data including meetings, transcripts, action items, and calendar. The user's timezone and display preferences are available as part of the workspace context.

## Trello
You are connected to the Trello MCP server. To identify the current user, call the `trelloReadMember` tool with `action: "get_me"` — it returns the authenticated user's Trello profile.

Dates & times: all date-time fields are UTC ISO 8601 (e.g. "2026-06-01T17:00:00.000Z"). This covers `due` on trelloWriteCard and trelloWriteInbox (card due dates), and `start`/`end` on trelloWritePlanner (calendar events). For local or relative times (e.g. "Friday 5pm"), convert to UTC using the user's timezone: for cards and Inbox, call trelloReadMember ("get_me") for `prefs.timezone`; for planner events, call trelloReadPlanner ("get") for `primaryCalendar.timezone`. When a date is given with no time, default to 09:00 in the user's local timezone.

Inbox: the Inbox is a personal quick-capture surface, not a normal board. To view or manage it, use trelloReadInbox and trelloWriteInbox — do not use trelloReadBoard to list or find Inbox cards.

Ordered creation: when creating multiple lists or cards that must keep a specific order, set `pos` to sequential integers (1, 2, 3, …) in the intended order — per list for cards, and across the board for lists. Each position is a distinct value, so lists and cards can be created in parallel without their positions colliding.

input.textContent:
# AD TRACKING SPEC — Full-funnel attribution (ad → lead → booked → showed → qualified → closed)
Written 2026-08-10. Goal: know exactly which ad/campaign/split-test produced every
lead, and which ones produce QUALIFIED booked calls, shows, and closes — not just clicks.

## WHAT EXISTS NOW (built 2026-08-10 in Notion)

- **Ad Scoreboard** database (under Client Tracking Command Center): one row per
  campaign/ad/split-test. Fields: Level, Meta ID, Funnel, Status, Spend to Date,
  Attributed Leads (relation), Lead Count (rollup), Cash Collected (rollup of
  Deal Value), Stages (rollup listing each attributed lead's stage), Notes.
  Seeded with all 9 known campaigns (spend from the 8/9 Meta pulls, windows
  documented per row) + the one verified ad: 120249661985200556 → Jill P. $15K.
- **Clients & Leads** additions: "Attributed Ad" (relation to Scoreboard) and
  "Attribution Confidence" select: Verified (GHL UTM) / Verified (Ad ID) /
  Derived / Missing. Blank = Missing. Only Jill P. is attributed so far.
- Funnel math per ad = its Attributed Leads' stages (booked/showed/offer/closed
  via the Stages rollup + Qualified Flag on each lead) against its Spend.

## THE PIPE (how attribution flows automatically going forward)

Meta ad → click URL carries UTMs → funnel page → GHL captures attribution on the
contact → booking → GHL Slack alert includes the UTMs → Notion lead row linked to
its Ad Scoreboard row at intake. Three wiring steps, one-time:

### Step 1 — Meta: standardized URL parameters on EVERY ad (do once per ad account)
In Ads Manager, at the AD level, "URL parameters" field (applies to all ads —
new ads inherit if set in the template/duplicated ads; verify on each launch):

    utm_source=meta&utm_medium=paid&utm_campaign={{campaign.name}}&utm_term={{adset.name}}&utm_content={{ad.name}}&campaign_id={{campaign.id}}&adset_id={{adset.id}}&ad_id={{ad.id}}

Meta fills the {{...}} dynamically — so every split test variant self-labels with
zero per-ad work. This is the single highest-leverage step: without it, GHL can
only attribute to fbclid/first-page, not the exact ad.

### Step 2 — GHL: capture + surface (needs Alan or a local Claude Code session; READ-ONLY rule waived only for these two config writes, with Alan's approval)
1. Confirm GHL attribution capture is on (Settings → it auto-stores First/Latest
   Attribution incl. utm_* and fbclid on form/calendar submissions — verify the
   funnel forms pass query strings; if the funnel has an intermediate page,
   ensure params persist to the booking widget).
2. Edit the "booked call" Slack notification (the LeadConnector workflow that
   posts to #alan-nguyen-booked-calls). Append to the message body:

       Campaign: {{contact.attributionSource.utm_campaign}}
       Ad Set: {{contact.attributionSource.utm_term}}
       Ad: {{contact.attributionSource.utm_content}}
       Ad ID: {{contact.attributionSource.utm_ad_id}} (field name per GHL: check attribution object; fallback {{contact.last_attribution_source}})

   From then on the Slack ledger is self-attributing — every future booking
   alert names its exact ad, and Notion intake copies it into Attributed Ad +
   Ad ID with Confidence = Verified (GHL UTM). No more reconstruction.

### Step 3 — Backfill the 54 existing leads (GHL export, extends GHL_EXPORT_SPEC_for_notion_backfill.md)
Add these columns to the export, per contact:

    utm_source, utm_campaign, utm_term (adset), utm_content (ad name),
    campaign_id, adset_id, ad_id, fbclid, session_source,
    first_attribution_date, latest_attribution_date

Then (any Claude session): match contact → Notion row → link Attributed Ad to
the matching Scoreboard row (create ad-level rows as new ad_ids appear), set
Ad ID + Attribution Confidence = Verified (GHL UTM). Contacts with no UTM data
(referrals like Bryan, organic) get Source set accordingly + Confidence noted.

## METRIC DEFINITIONS (per Scoreboard row, weekly)

- Leads = Lead Count rollup. Booked+ = leads at stage Booked Call or beyond.
- Shows = stages in {Showed, Offer Made, Closed Won, Nurture-after-show}.
- Qualified shows = shows with Qualified Flag true (720+/income rules already
  encoded in Clients & Leads).
- Closes / Cash = Closed Won count / Cash Collected rollup.
- Efficiency: CPL, cost/booked, cost/show, cost/qualified-show, cost/close, ROAS
  = each = Spend to Date ÷ the count (compute in weekly review; spend refreshed
  from Meta dailies or the Meta connector when reconnected — it was disconnected
  from the 8/10 cloud session).

## SPLIT TESTS

Name variants explicitly in Meta (e.g. "W2-VSL-A | blue-suit" vs "W2-VSL-B |
UGC") — utm_content={{ad.name}} then separates them automatically. In the
Scoreboard, create one row per variant (Level = Split Test or Ad), Meta ID =
ad_id. The winner is read off cost/qualified-show and cost/close, not CTR.

## KNOWN GAPS (honest state, 2026-08-10)

- 53 of 54 leads have NO ad-level attribution yet (only Jill P.). Blocked on
  Step 3 (GHL export) — the data exists in GHL, nothing else holds it.
- Spend figures are documented-window sums, not lifetime (pre-6/19 spend not
  broken out per campaign anywhere accessible; W25-W29 total $5,592 known).
- Medical attribution question folds into this: once UTMs are on contacts,
  "did any Medical-campaign click ever book?" becomes a one-line query.
- Meta Ads connector disconnected mid-session; live spend sync resumes when it
  or the local dailies are available.

## TRACKER TASK
Follow-Up created in Notion (due 8/11): "Wire full ad attribution" — the three
steps above. Steps 1-2 are ~15 minutes in Ads Manager + GHL; Step 3 rides the
existing GHL pull.

## What exists now

**Ad Scoreboard** — new database under the Client Tracking Command Center, one row per campaign/ad/split-test. Each row shows: spend to date, attributed leads (linked to the real client records), lead count, the stage of every attributed lead (booked/showed/offer/closed at a glance), and cash collected — so "which ad produces qualified shows and closes, not just clicks" is read directly off the row. Seeded with all 9 known campaigns with their documented spend/CPC/CTR, plus the one ad-level attribution that's already verified: **ad 120249661985200556 → Jill P. → $15,000**.

**Clients & Leads** got two new fields: **Attributed Ad** (relation to the scoreboard) and **Attribution Confidence** (Verified GHL-UTM / Verified Ad-ID / Derived / Missing) — so verified attribution never mixes with guesses.

## The honest gap, and the fix

**53 of 54 leads have no ad-level attribution yet** — that data exists only inside GHL (it auto-captures UTMs per contact), and the Slack booking alerts don't currently carry it. Three one-time wiring steps make every future lead self-attributing and backfill the past:

1. **Meta (~5 min):** set the standardized URL-parameter string on the ad account — `utm_campaign={{campaign.name}}&utm_content={{ad.name}}&ad_id={{ad.id}}`… Meta fills these dynamically, so **every split-test variant labels itself automatically forever**.
2. **GHL (~10 min, needs your approval since it's a GHL write):** add the attribution fields to the booked-call Slack notification template — from then on every booking alert names its exact ad, and the Slack ledger becomes self-attributing.
3. **Backfill:** the existing GHL export now needs the UTM columns (added to the spec) — one pull attributes all 54 existing leads as Verified (GHL UTM).

A Follow-Up is in Notion due tomorrow tracking those three steps. Two caveats logged: spend figures are documented-window sums (pre-6/19 per-campaign spend isn't broken out anywhere accessible), and the Meta Ads connector dropped from this session mid-way, so live spend refresh resumes when it's reconnected or via your local dailies. Once step 3 runs, the Medical-attribution mystery also collapses into a one-line query: "did any Medical-campaign click ever book?"

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

export const meta = {
  name: 'apw-mastery-system',
  description: 'Build the APW organized mastery system: imports, call library, SOPs, sales patterns, data completeness, views, then audit',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Build', detail: '6 parallel workstreams' },
    { title: 'Audit', detail: 'verify + update Master Checklist' },
  ],
}

const IDS = {
  clients: 'collection://5614ffa0-e3d0-40cb-ae64-b32ec52e288c',
  comms: 'collection://09c1e23f-9c55-468f-b4f2-19c7fe011477',
  documents: 'collection://725de51f-afb9-49ba-b121-d325dc33acb1',
  callLib: 'collection://51af1527-a898-480a-94e1-14c28f396da0',
  sopLib: 'collection://9f07f2d4-493f-4d66-9d91-3195ab28d6f8',
  checklist: 'collection://377886f5-f8e6-492b-8099-10f9c8943a96',
  hubPage: '3b75bb1ffef48196aa4efcf029dc732d',
  bulkFolder: '1wncereH-vBChO-wUqtvw87SBeqyPRt5P',
}

const COMMON = 'Workspace: Alan Nguyen\'s "Ascend Prime Wealth" Notion. Use ToolSearch to load Notion MCP tools (notion-fetch, notion-query-data-sources, notion-create-pages, notion-update-page, notion-create-view) and other MCP tools you need. Rules: NEVER delete or overwrite existing content - Notes/text fields are append-only (preserve existing text, add " || 8/10 systems pass: ..."); never invent data (empty beats guessed); never downgrade a client Stage. Clients & Leads data source: ' + IDS.clients + ' (64 rows; query url, Client, Email, Stage, Notes via SQL). Comms Log: ' + IDS.comms + ' (~140 rows). Return a compact factual report of counts + gaps as your final text.'

phase('Build')
const lanes = await parallel([
  () => agent(COMMON + ' TASK (drive-files-importer): The Drive folder "APW Bulk 08.10.2026" id ' + IDS.bulkFolder + ' holds Alan\'s PC client files (credit reports, disputes, etc.), owned by support@ascendprimewealth.com, currently link-shared only. STEP 1: test access - search_files with query parentId = \'' + IDS.bulkFolder + '\'. If empty, wait and retry once, then report "STILL BLOCKED - folder not enumerable; needs direct share to nguyenalan95@gmail.com" and stop (do not mark anything done). If accessible: recursively enumerate all subfolders/files, then index EVERY file into the Documents db (' + IDS.documents + ' - fetch schema first; ~11 rows exist, dedupe by URL/title): title = file name, Drive link, client relation matched from folder/file name to the 64 clients (First name + Last initial matching), doc type select (credit report / dispute / agreement / other per schema options that actually exist), and note files that match no client. Organization requirement: files must be findable per client - the client relation is what groups them; verify each client with files shows them on their client page.', { label: 'drive-files', phase: 'Build' }),
  () => agent(COMMON + ' TASK (gmail-comms-sweep): Connected Gmail is nguyenalan95@gmail.com (personal - most client mail lives in the UNCONNECTED support@ mailbox; expect thin results, that is fine). Query Clients & Leads for all rows with Email filled (~55). For each, search Gmail (mcp__Gmail__search_threads, query "{from:EMAIL to:EMAIL}") - batch sensibly. For every real client thread found: create a Comms Log row (' + IDS.comms + ', fetch schema first): title "Email — <subject>", Channel=Email, direction per sender, date = thread date, client relation, snippet in summary field. Dedupe against existing rows. Also search the two known client-adjacent threads: Ed Choi (edwenchoy/choi emails) and any thread from theloschfamily09. Report per-client hit counts and total rows created, plus explicit note that support@ mailbox remains the gap.', { label: 'gmail-sweep', phase: 'Build' }),
  () => agent(COMMON + ' TASK (call-librarian): Build the complete Call Library (' + IDS.callLib + ' - fetch schema; currently empty). Use Fathom list_meetings with include_summary:true across 2026-03-01 to 2026-08-11 (max_pages until exhausted, ~130 meetings). Create ONE row per recording: Title (use client name if identifiable, else original title + date), date:Date:start, Fathom URL, Type select (Sales Call / No-Show Dial / Client Fulfillment / Team / Coaching / Partner / Ops / Onboarding - judge from summary), Client relation where the meeting matches one of the 64 (match by title name, invitee email vs client Email column, or summary), Summary = condensed AI summary (max ~800 chars), Outcome = one line (showed/no-show/signed/rejected/etc. if evident). Batch create-pages up to 100/call. If Notion rate-limits (the plan has query limits), slow down and use view-mode queries or smaller batches - do not abandon; report any rows you could not create. Report: total rows, breakdown by Type, how many have Client relations.', { label: 'call-library', phase: 'Build' }),
  () => agent(COMMON + ' TASK (sop-architect): Deep-dive all SOPs and build the SOP Library (' + IDS.sopLib + ' - fetch schema; empty). SOURCES: (1) notion-search for existing SOPs (Lynn built a fulfillment SOP section with timestamps over Alan\'s Loom videos - find it); (2) Fathom team/coaching call summaries 2026-06-15 onward (list_meetings include_summary) - they are dense with process decisions: setter triage script + credit-report "soft pull / Tri-Merged" script, objection handling (Edify-Defer-Reframe, Aikido), Slack emoji status system, follow-up cadence (double-dial 1-2x/day), Trello logging conventions, dispute workflow (Credit Karma -> bureau dispute center -> PDF template; CFPB escalation; 4-day legal window script), client onboarding (live onboarding call, GHL agreement+LPOA combined, credit logins via GHL), booking hygiene (private browsing to avoid contact merges, manual booking outside 72h window), pricing tiers ($8k/$6k/$4k/$2k + guarantee framing); (3) Slack ops messages if useful. BUILD: one SOP Library row per procedure with page content = the actual SOP (steps, scripts verbatim where available, do/don\'t), Area + Audience selects, Status = "Existing - verified" (if it exists in Notion already - link it) or "Drafted 2026-08-10", Sources field = fathom/notion links. Mark clear gaps as Status "Gap - to create" rows with a description of what is missing (e.g. Loom transcripts inaccessible). ALSO create a single page titled "START HERE — New Hire Guide" as a child of page ' + IDS.hubPage + ': role-based orientation (Setter / Fulfillment / Closer), linking the SOP Library, Call Library, Clients & Leads, Comms Log, Master Ops Checklist, with a 1-day and 1-week ramp checklist. New hires complain about disorganization - this page is the fix; make it genuinely clear. Report: SOP rows by status, gaps list, START HERE page url.', { label: 'sop-architect', phase: 'Build' }),
  () => agent(COMMON + ' TASK (sales-analyst): Produce the closer-training sales-pattern analysis. STEP 1 - find the "Constantine frameworks": search Krisp (mcp__Krisp__search_meeting_content / search_meetings) for "Constantine", search Google Drive fullText for "Constantine", Slack search, and Fathom search_meetings. Document what you find (a sales coach/framework Alan references); if truly not found, say so explicitly and proceed without it. STEP 2 - analyze outcomes from Fathom summaries (transcripts max 3, only where decisive): WON: Ed Choi ($2K, 6/29-7/1), Jill P. ($15K, W28), Leo D. ($12K, 8/8 - burned-by-others trust framing won), Joe S. ($5K offer accepted-ish), Ashwini A. (onboarding); LOST/STALLED: Ghani A. (rejected SPV strategy - broker mismatch), Chris B. (paused - affordability), Pradeep B. (money tight, $300 micro-commitment), George J. (offer no follow-up), Zacherly S. (competitor comparison pending); NO-SHOWS (11). Extract patterns: what language/structure closes (transparency framing, best/worst case, refundable deposit + guarantee, asking for more upfront, micro-commitments), what loses (ego-resistance to aged entities, broker-expectation mismatch, price-first prospects), objection playbook, discovery quality markers. STEP 3 - write "Closer Training — Sales Patterns & Playbook" as a row/page in the SOP Library (' + IDS.sopLib + ', Area "Sales / Setting", Audience "Closer", Status "Drafted 2026-08-10") citing every claim with its fathom link, including a section aligning patterns to the Constantine framework if found. Report: framework verdict, top 5 win-patterns, top 3 loss-patterns, page url.', { label: 'sales-analyst', phase: 'Build' }),
  () => agent(COMMON + ' TASK (data-completeness + views): PART 1: Fill every DERIVABLE empty field on the 64 client rows. Sources: each client\'s "Booking alert" Comms Log row summaries (form answers: funding ask range, credit score band, income range, employment, business type) + existing Notes. Mappings: Score Band select from form ("720-749"->"720+"? NO - use exact schema options: 720+ / 680-719 / <680 / Unknown; "750-799","800+","720-749" -> "720+", "Less than 720" -> Unknown unless range known, "680-719"->"680-719", "Less than 679"-><680); Income Range direct map; Employment map (W2 Employee->W2, Active Business->Business Owner, Unemployed->Unemployed, Retirement/SSI/VA->Unknown but note it); Funnel = "Professionals-BizOwners" for every funnel-booked lead (all alerts were W2/BizOwner calendar) EXCEPT medical-profile leads already marked Medical; Source = "Meta Ad" for all funnel-booked leads lacking Source (NOT Bryan - referral-derived, leave); Funding Ask NUMBER only where a specific figure exists in Notes (e.g. Bryan 1400000 done, Gunjan 300000-350000 -> leave number empty, note range) - never store a guessed midpoint; date:Last Touch:start = latest Comms Log row date for that client if later than current value. Do NOT touch Stage, Deal Value, Email, Phone. PART 2: create curated views (notion-create-view; read notion://docs/view-dsl-spec via notion-fetch first): on Clients & Leads database - "Pipeline Board" (board grouped by Stage), "By Ad Source" (table grouped by Attributed Ad or Source, showing attribution fields), "Revenue" (table filtered Stage=Closed Won or Deal Value not empty, sorted Deal Value desc), "Data Gaps" (table filtered any of Email/Phone/Score Band/Income Range empty - approximate with the DSL\'s abilities), "Follow-Ups Due" (table sorted Next Follow-Up asc, filtered not empty); on Documents db - "By Client" grouped by client relation; on Comms Log - "By Client" grouped by client; on Call Library - "By Type" grouped by Type. Report: fields filled per column (counts), fields left empty because not derivable (needs GHL), views created with names.', { label: 'completeness-views', phase: 'Build' }),
])

phase('Audit')
const summaries = lanes.map((r, i) => 'LANE ' + i + ': ' + (r ? String(r).slice(0, 2500) : 'FAILED/SKIPPED')).join('\n\n')
const audit = await agent(COMMON + ' TASK (auditor): Six build lanes just ran. Their self-reports: \n' + summaries + '\n\nVERIFY independently (do not trust reports blindly): query row counts in Call Library (' + IDS.callLib + '), SOP Library (' + IDS.sopLib + '), Comms Log, Documents; spot-check 3 client rows for filled selects + appended-not-overwritten Notes; confirm the START HERE page exists under page ' + IDS.hubPage + '. Then UPDATE the Master Ops Checklist (' + IDS.checklist + '): for each In Progress row matching these lanes (Gmail comms sweep, Call Library, SOP deep dive, Sales-pattern analysis, New-hire START HERE, Data completeness, Curated views, Client files import, Auditor pass) set Status to Done ONLY where verified, keep In Progress/Blocked otherwise, and append the verified evidence (counts/links) to its Evidence / Links field. The "Client files import" row stays "Blocked - Alan" if the Drive lane reported STILL BLOCKED. Finally set the "Auditor pass" row itself to Done with a one-line summary. Return: the verified counts table, discrepancies between lane reports and reality, and the definitive remaining-gaps list.', { label: 'auditor', phase: 'Audit', effort: 'high' })

return { lanes, audit }

## Control structures (live now, on the Command Center)

- **[Master Ops Checklist](https://app.notion.com/p/43852d864f7b4977976d6be6a3ec1d30)** — 31 items covering *everything* asked this entire session, each with Area, Owner, Status (Done / In Progress / Blocked-Alan / Blocked-GHL / Open), and a **Verification column defining what "done" means** — this is the self-checking layer you asked for. 7 already Done with evidence links.
- **[Call Library](https://app.notion.com/p/4a3dd72b984f427e8b421c681a9873f0)** — every Fathom recording: date, type, client, link, summary, outcome, analyzed-flag.
- **[SOP Library](https://app.notion.com/p/a7475e83230a49f894467b1c742c446e)** — procedures by Area + Audience (Setter/Closer/Fulfillment), with Status distinguishing verified-existing vs drafted vs gap.

## The agent fleet (running now — 6 build lanes + auditor)

Role mapping to your ask: I'm the **director/architect** (structure + orchestration), the workflow script is the **planner/manager**, six specialist **executors** run in parallel, and a dedicated **auditor** independently verifies counts, spot-checks that nothing was overwritten, and flips checklist statuses only where verified:

1. **drive-files-importer** — your PC client files → Documents db, per-client
2. **gmail-comms-sweep** — client email threads → Comms Log
3. **call-librarian** — all ~130 recordings → Call Library
4. **sop-architect** — existing SOPs (incl. Lynn's) + process content mined from every coaching call → full SOP Library + **"START HERE — New Hire Guide"** (the direct fix for the disorganization complaints: role-based, 1-day/1-week ramp)
5. **sales-analyst** — hunts the Constantine framework across Krisp/Drive/Slack/Fathom, analyzes won vs lost calls, writes the closer-training playbook with every claim cited to a recording
6. **completeness-views** — your mid-turn ask: fills every derivable field (score band, income, employment, funnel, source, last-touch) from the booking-alert data, and builds the curated views: **Pipeline Board, By Ad Source, Revenue, Data Gaps, Follow-Ups Due**, plus **grouped-by-client views on Documents and Comms** — so each client page reads as one organized folder, not a wall.

## Your 3 clicks (gating real data)

1. **"APW Bulk 08.10.2026" folder** → Share → add **nguyenalan95@gmail.com** as Viewer — it's owned by support@ and link-shared, so the connector can see the door but not inside. The import agent retests automatically.
2. **support@ascendprimewealth.com** isn't connected anywhere — that's where client email actually lives, so the Gmail sweep will be thin until it's added as a connector.
3. **Loom** has no connector — export transcripts to Drive (or paste into Notion) and the SOP agent mines them next pass.

## Master suggestions (the "anything else")

- **The single highest-leverage unlock remains the GHL pull** — it closes 6 checklist items at once.
- **Weekly self-audit**: once this run lands, I'd put the auditor on a weekly Routine so the checklist never rots. Say the word.
- **Notion bottleneck**: the plan's SQL-query metering is the only real limit hit today; agents are instructed to batch and degrade gracefully. If the audit reports throttling, the Business-plan upgrade is the clean fix — otherwise ignore.
- **Passwords**: restating for the securing pass — bureau logins stay in GHL, team credentials belong in a password manager, not Notion.

Full verified counts and the definitive gap list arrive when the auditor reports.

# MASTER CLOSING FRAMEWORK — Grand Slam Sequence

Drafted 2026-08-10. Built exclusively from Constantine's written structure, the Alan+Constantine coaching sessions (Krisp), and real won/lost APW call recordings (Fathom). Every step cites its source. Companion doc: Closer Training — Sales Patterns & Playbook (Notion, 3b95bb1ffef48138a6e1cb3a0a90d880).

## How to read this
Constantine's architecture is **Intro/Frame → Discovery → Transition → Pitch → Close**. The design principle behind every step, in his words from the Sales Structure doc: Discovery exists to get "a) the information we need that is relevant to what we will pitch, b) reveal emotional leverage for the prospect to take action now, c) build rapport, and d) **eliminate objections before the close**." The close is not where objections are fought — it is where a properly-run call has already made them impossible. "One of the primary emotions that you need the prospect to feel → is **safety**: reassurance, belonging, comfort."

# PART I — INTRO / FRAME (2–5 min)

## Step 1 — Welcome + Location
**Purpose:** Human first contact; get them talking about something zero-stakes.
**Script (verbatim, Ghani call):** "So — where are you calling from?" …then relate genuinely ("Not too far away. I was in the Irvine area not too long ago.").
**Pre-handles:** Cold-formality / guardedness. A prospect who has answered two easy questions is already in answering rhythm before any sensitive question arrives.
**Source:** Sales Structure doc ("Welcome, location, source, why us"); Ghani 6:15 (fathom.video/calls/746607489).

## Step 2 — Source + Motivation (harvest self-sold data)
**Purpose:** Make the prospect state, in their own words, why they came. First plank of the pre-sold mechanism.
**Script:** "How did you end up finding us? Was it through an ad or a referral?" → "And what motivated you to reach out?" Then per the doc: "quick acknowledgement of what they said (**self sold data**) → transition to frame."
**Pre-handles:** "Why am I on this call?" and later think-about-it stalls — their stated motivation becomes callback ammunition for the pitch and close.
**Source:** Doc "Source" section; Ghani 6:47–7:29 ("you said you guarantee to find somebody… perfect fit" — his expectation surfaced in minute one; see Failure Mode 1).

## Step 3 — Permission-Based "Why Us" (credibility by metrics, not credentials)
**Purpose:** Establish authority through numbers before any pitch exists.
**Script (verbatim, Ghani 8:38–10:19):** "Before we get started, would it be helpful if I gave you a little bit of a background on the company as well as the agenda for the call?" → origin story: "I had a medical incident… it destroyed my credit… I ended up having a 500 credit score. And eventually, over time, I learned how to transform that 500 credit score to over 500K in funding… We've been in business since 2023… we've generated, using our systems, over $10 million in funding." Close the loop: "Was that context helpful, before we get started?"
Constantine's rule (6/17 session): "It's good, but it needs to be **tied to more metrics**… you want to talk about $500K plus in funding and growing… I've been doing this for X number of years… X number of clients and counting." And no name-dropping here — "detailed stories only if directly relevant… that's too much."
**Pre-handles:** "Are you certified/licensed?" — the answer is pre-loaded as track record vs paper ("contrast paper certificate vs track record, $10M+ funded," 7/15 coaching, fathom.video/calls/748467538). Also pre-handles burned-before: "helping many who have been routinely let down by the mass funding companies… that routinely over promise and under deliver" (doc, About Us).
**Source:** Doc "Clean" intro §4; Krisp 6/17; Ghani transcript.

## Step 4 — Strong Frame: pressure-off agenda + definitive yes-or-no contract
**Purpose:** Remove sales pressure AND contract for a decision — the single highest-leverage pre-handle in the system.
**Script (verbatim, doc):** "The purpose of this call is to walk through our process, to see if we are a good fit for one another, and to see if we can actually help you. If we can → we can discuss details later in the call. And if not → we will do our best to point you in the right direction — no big deal, and no hard feelings either way; we'll part ways as friends regardless… So all that I ask, is that by the end of the call, out of respect to both of us, you're able to give me a simple **definitive yes, or no**. Does that sound good to you?"
Live version that worked (Ghani 10:21): "…if we deem it's a good fit, we can discuss what it looks like moving forward. And if it's not, no big deal — either way, we'll point you in the right direction. Does that sound good?"
**Pre-handles:** (1) "I need to think about it" — they agreed up front to a yes/no; you can later invoke that agreement without being pushy. (2) Burned-before distrust — "for prospects burned by others, use a 'no pressure' frame to rebuild trust" (7/17 coaching, fathom.video/calls/751792038); this frame preceded the Leo $12K signature (8/8, fathom.video/calls/777554648).
**Source:** Doc "Strong frame"; Fathom 7/17.

## Step 5 — Partner Reconfirmation Checkpoint
**Purpose:** Confirm every decision-maker is present BEFORE investing 60 minutes.
**Script (verbatim, doc §5.5):** "Just before we get started, I wanted to confirm quickly… everyone is on the call that would be needed for financials, such as the PG, treasurer, partners, etc… just you? Or?"
Constantine's placement rule (6/10 session): partner qualification belongs in **triage**; the closing call gets only "a quick partner reconfirmation checkpoint at the start… before the Discovery/strong frame section" — "cold-opening with it risks triggering ego-defensive responses," so triage asks the low-friction "are your partners on the same page with funding?" inside the goals section.
**Pre-handles:** "I need to talk to my spouse/partner" — killed an hour before it could be said. Deeper version in discovery: "Who else would be involved? …Based on their roles → what are their goals? (get everyone's buy-in by speaking to **their** problems and goals)" (doc, Partner section).
**Source:** Doc §5.5 + Partner; Krisp 6/10.

# PART II — DISCOVERY (20–30 min)

## Step 6 — Main Challenge + Business Background
**Purpose:** Label their specific problem; understand the flow of money.
**Script (doc):** "If everything was perfect in your business right now, we wouldn't be speaking… so what is the main challenge or bottleneck in your business?" / "Tell me about your business — what do you do? How does it work? How does it operate?" If vague: "Aside from X, what else?" / "Can you expand on that?" / "What do you mean by that specifically?" Use **impact questions**: "when you see an opportunity to expose the impact of what they're telling you… ask a curious question so they can describe that specific impact."
**Frame it first** (6/3 session): "open the discovery by telling prospects that background questions will determine **whether funding is even the right path** — even if their credit qualifies." This "positions Alan as the decision-maker on fit, giving him authority and reducing resistance to non-credit questions."
**Pre-handles:** Value objections — a prospect who has described their own bottleneck in detail cannot later claim the problem isn't worth solving.
**Source:** Doc Discovery §1–2; Krisp 6/3.

## Step 7 — Money Block: amount, allocation, why funding
**Purpose:** Get the numbers the pitch will run on and the ROI the price will be compared against.
**Script:** "How much funding are you looking for?" → "How do you plan on investing that funding?" → "**Why** — how would it benefit you and change things for the better, specifically?" → "What would the funding allow you to do that you wouldn't be able to do without it — present and future?" (both sub-questions added in the 6/3 session). Pullback preframe (doc): "Not all companies require funding… so I just want to figure out if you actually do need funding… I want to make sure I'm recommending something you actually need."
**Pre-handles:** Price. When the use of funds is quantified (Ghani itemized ~$50K licensing + staff runway unprompted; Ashwini's $232K/yr interest, fathom.video/calls/764436554), the fee is later compared against their number, not against zero.
**Source:** Doc Money; Ghani 11:02–15:32.

## Step 8 — Runway Stretch (upsize the goal with a client-preframe)
**Purpose:** Expand the target — bigger goal, bigger urgency, bigger fee base.
**Script (verbatim, Ghani 15:48–18:11):** "Typically, a lot of the clients we work with, when they're budgeting for funding, they're not looking too far ahead… or factoring in the unknown variables… We suggest calculating at least six, if not 18 months worth of runway." → "How much funding would you need to secure to create six months of runway?" (Ghani: $150–200K became "$400K to be comfortable" in ninety seconds.) This is the doc's preframe pattern: "talk about other clients and what they would do → tie it back into a clarification question."
**Pre-handles:** "The amount you can get me isn't worth the fee" — they set the bigger number themselves.
**Source:** Ghani transcript; doc Background/preframe.

## Step 9 — Credit Qualification (with the three-fold rationale preframe)
**Purpose:** Qualify hard numbers; justify sensitive questions before asking them.
**Script (6/3 + doc):** "Now I'm going to shift into credit — the reason why is so we can know **if** we can actually fund you, **how much**, and **how fast**." Then: score per bureau; highest single-card limit ("10k plus preferred, 5k acceptable, 2500 bare minimum" — doc); 3–5 tradelines; 2+ years age; no delinquencies/derogs; utilization; inquiries per bureau; business age/standing/ownership. Live standard (Ed close): every number on the table — 767/788/788, 22+ accounts, >30% utilization being paid down, 7/8/1 inquiries, prior $80K stack, Chase/Amex blacklist.
**Pre-handles:** Post-sale surprises and guarantee disputes — the 7/1 pricing session flagged that "a deal was quoted before a full credit report review, revealing undisclosed issues post-sale." Secure the report pre-call (setter checklist step 10, doc; 7/22 session: the ask is reframed as an act of helping — "without it, prospects can't get funded by anyone").
**Source:** Doc Qualification; Krisp 6/3 + 7/22; Ed transcript (fathom.video/calls/728895030).

## Step 10 — Efforts + How Long (stretch pain; mine their failures)
**Purpose:** Surface what they've tried, so the pitch is positioned against their own lived failures.
**Script:** "Have you ever tried to get funding in the past?" (the 6/3 bridge question from credit → efforts). Follow the Ed pattern (12:09–16:26): "Did you work with a company or do it yourself?" → "Why didn't you continue with them?" → "Then you tried on your own — what were the results?" → Ed: "**It was a disaster. No success at all.**"
**Pre-handles:** DIY-ego AND burned-before, simultaneously. Ed convicted himself: company got him $80K but only once; solo attempt failed. The pitch then only had to be "the thing that fixes what you already told me failed." Constantine's unsell backup for know-it-alls: "agree they probably could, then expose one flaw in their logic for the aha moment" (7/15, fathom.video/calls/748467538).
**Source:** Doc Efforts/How long; Ed transcript; Fathom 7/15.

## Step 11 — Expectation Check (the Ghani question)
**Purpose:** Confirm they understand WHAT we are — coaching/consulting with lender access — before an hour is invested.
**Script (built from the loss):** "Just so I set expectations properly — some people come to us expecting a licensed loan broker they can hand a package to. What we actually are is [coaching/consulting + lender database + done-for-you execution]. Which were you picturing?"
**Pre-handles:** The broker-expectation mismatch that killed Ghani at minute 60: "I thought that you have a pool of lenders… and you are a broker… I was going to delegate that task to you. But if… you are not endorsed with NMLS… **then I will pass on your services**" (1:07–1:08). Constantine's debrief: qualify urgency/authority/ability in the first 5 minutes (fathom.video/calls/739886841); this check should have run in triage (debrief, fathom.video/calls/748651348).
**Source:** Ghani transcript; 7/15 debrief.

## Step 12 — Bucket Discernment (prospect self-selects the offer)
**Purpose:** Have them choose their own delivery model — second plank of the pre-sold mechanism.
**Script (verbatim, Ghani 41:39–43:08):** "We have three buckets people typically fall in. Bucket one: 'I just want to do this myself — teach me.' Bucket two: 'I don't have time, I want you to do it for me.' Bucket three: hybrid — 'do it for me in the beginning, teach me along the way so I can fund myself forever.' Out of those three, which would you say you align with most?" Ed's version, assumptive (28:22): "Normally we have a program where we teach people how to do this themselves… but obviously you're super busy, so that doesn't sound like it would be for you, correct?" — "Correct."
**Pre-handles:** "I could do this myself." Whoever picks bucket 2/3 has conceded they want it done for them. **Danger signal:** bucket 1 + expert self-identity (Ghani: "I do not need coaching") = the Expert's Ego failure mode; pivot immediately to Step 26's countermove. Strategy note (6/17): pitch DFY as primary ("give them what the market wants"), training delivered at the end as differentiator — "the last thing we want them to leave the call with is the idea that they can look into this and do it on their own." Two competitive edges (6/10): no 10% funding fee (vs competitors' $10K–$25K+ on $100–250K deals) and future independence.
**Source:** Ghani + Ed transcripts; Krisp 6/17 + 6/10.

## Step 13 — Timing, Logistics & Commitment (future-pace + micro-agreement)
**Purpose:** Lock time commitment and "why now" before price exists.
**Script (doc):** "Do you feel like NOW is the right time — why now vs later?" "Is there anything that would get in the way of this — projects, vacations?" → "In terms of our most successful clients, they're able to tie in roughly 30–60 minutes per day on average consistently… Is this something you can realistically commit to?" Timing resistance → "Walk me through a typical day — you wake up at what time? …" Mindset preframe: "Our most successful clients understand the right mindset in how to interpret problems — and that's exactly what we teach. So what that means is, when XYZ inevitably happens, we coach you how to properly navigate those challenges so you don't get frustrated hitting walls."
**Pre-handles:** "Now's not the right time" and logistics smokescreens — both answered on record 30 minutes before the close (see Step 24's elimination walk).
**Source:** Doc Timing/Logistics/Commitment.

## Step 14 — Prompt for Missed Info
**Purpose:** Close discovery airtight.
**Script (doc):** "Is there anything else that I need to know about your business or background, in order to make the best recommendation for you?"
**Pre-handles:** Late-surfacing facts ("oh, by the way, I have a bankruptcy…") that would otherwise detonate in the close.
**Source:** Doc.

# PART III — TRANSITION

## Step 15 — Summary → Certainty Statement → Permission to Pitch
**Purpose:** Convert discovery into a fit-verdict, then get invited to pitch.
**Script (doc):** Summarize ("Accurate? What else do you want to add?") → "Based on everything that you've told me, **you fit the profile of our most successful clients**. So that being the case, I want to share our process with you from A-Z. Are you ready for me to go ahead with that?" The certainty statement is the industry critique: "I've personally gone through 100+ ads and offers from the leading companies… What I learned was: 1) it is WAY too common for these companies to OVER-promise and UNDER-deliver, 2) the marketing number is often not realistic (this is why we state a range vs a fixed amount), 3) the salespeople typically are NOT experienced in funding themselves — they sell the concept without first-hand knowledge of what gets people approved and denied in underwriting."
**Pre-handles:** Burned-before (we name the exact way they got burned, and structurally differ) and resistance-to-pitch (they said "yes, go ahead" — micro-agreement #3 of the ladder: frame-yes at Step 4, buckets at Step 12, permission here).
**Source:** Doc Transition.

# PART IV — PITCH (5–10 min)

## Step 16 — Preface: Outcome + Social Proof → "through this 3-stage process"
**Purpose:** Anchor the goal number, re-anchor credibility, open the staged walkthrough.
**Script (verbatim, doc Pitch Updated + 6/17 mock):** "So the goal is for us to secure ___ in funding. Now, the way we've done that for our clients — [500 → $500K+ personal; industry since 2023; $10M+ client funding] — is through a three-stage process…" Slides: max 1–2 per stage, bullets only — "you do most of the explaining… if following along becomes inundation, they feel overwhelmed" (Constantine, 6/17).
**Pre-handles:** Uncertainty/trust — the #1 close-killer in Constantine's four-category model.
**Source:** Doc; Krisp 6/17.

## Step 17 — Stage 1 Credit Optimization: Callback → Solution → Benefit → Prompt
**Purpose:** First proof of expertise, customized with their own numbers.
**Script:** Callback (6/17 mock): "So earlier you told me you have a 750 credit score, more than three cards, your highest limit is at least $10K — you have a strong profile…" Solution: names/addresses/employers cleanup, inquiry removal, utilization to 1–7% ("the mere fact that I'm referring back to what you told me in discovery makes the thing feel like it's more for me" — Constantine, 6/17). Benefit (doc, verbatim): "→ **OPTIMIZED FOR FUNDING — AUTOMATED HIGH-LIMIT APPROVALS**, instead of low limits, long delays, and denials." The silver-platter frame that landed live: "we're bringing them your credit report on a golden silver platter" → Ghani himself completed it: "**So they have every reason to say yes, no reason to say no**" (32:42). Prompt: "So that's stage one. What questions do you have on that specifically?" / "How are you feeling so far?"
**Pre-handles:** DIY-ego (underwriting nuance = expertise moat) and "why do you need all this" — every deliverable is tied to a fact they gave you.
**Source:** Doc Pitch Updated; Krisp 6/17; Ghani + Ed transcripts.

## Step 18 — Stage 2 Funding Strategy & Approvals → Prompt
**Script:** "Then we build your **customized funding sequence** — specific to your geolocation and your specific profile — exactly where we're going to go, what we're going to say, what we're going to do" (Ghani 39:20: "capital sequencing plan"). Differentiation data point: "ASCEND's 12,000+ data-point database to target institutions" (P Reddy 8/10, fathom.video/calls/777298604). Prompt for questions again.
**Pre-handles:** "What am I actually paying for?" — the strategy layer is the thing DIY can't replicate (Step 10's admission).

## Step 19 — Stage 3 Execution & Advanced Strategies → Wrap
**Script:** "The final stage is the one everyone loves — the approvals. We're working advanced strategies and compounding results to your $___ goal, and eventually $___" (Ghani 40:06). Wrap: "math"/outcome + confidence social-proof statement (doc). Ed's live wrap (27:35): "So from what you understand about us taking you through credit optimization, to the custom strategy specifically for you and your geolocation, to the funding itself, with inquiry removal throughout — what questions do you have about any of those steps?"
**Pre-handles:** Process uncertainty — three prompts across three stages means no doubt survives to the close unspoken.

## Step 20 — Temp Check 1–10: the prospect self-sells
**Purpose:** The keystone of the pre-sold mechanism — they argue FOR the program.
**Script (verbatim, doc):** "How are you feeling on the whole process, on a scale of 1–10?" **If 8+:** "That's great — what do you feel would be especially beneficial or helpful?" **If below 8:** "What would make you a 10?" ("you have to get their certainty up… you need them to tell you, and sell themselves on why.")
**Pre-handles:** "I need to think about it" — the thinking happens here, out loud, with you in the room. **Signal discipline:** Ghani deflected the temp check ("Words are not an indicative of performance… I'm 100% okay with everything you said" — 50:58) and refused testimonials; an evasive temp-check answer means certainty is NOT built — loop back, do not proceed to price. P Reddy answered "7/10" and stalled into "I need to research you" (8/10) — the 7 was the tell; "what would make you a 10" is mandatory, not optional.
**Source:** Doc Rank-on-Scale; Ghani + P Reddy calls.

## Step 21 — Next Steps / Future Pace (x → y → z)
**Script (verbatim, Ed 32:06):** "The process after this is: we get the agreement signed, we do the payment, and then we get you into onboarding — it'll just run you through a bunch of really easy videos." Doc: 10–15 seconds, "day 0 → onboarding… day X this… day B…"
**Pre-handles:** Fear of the unknown post-yes. Saying yes now has a picture attached.

## Step 22 — Investment: the Grand Slam Offer Assembly
**Purpose:** Present price as a de-risked, ROI-positive, transparent structure. Order (doc): **value stack → ROI → price drop → silence.**
**The five components, all field-proven:**
1. **Refundable deposit + funding guarantee** (Ed 29:10, verbatim): "It's just $2,000 up front… which is refundable if $20,000 minimum in funding is not secured — which would be a 10x return… Does that make sense so far?" Engineered deliberately on 7/1 (fathom.video/calls/731966182): "full refund guarantee to de-risk the offer." Current calibration: $5K deposit / $50K floor (P Reddy).
2. **Best case / worst case framing** (7/1): "Best case: you invest upfront, receive significant funding, the fee becomes irrelevant. Worst case: full refund, **plus** a detailed explanation of why funding failed to guide your next move." Either way they win — the no-lose geometry.
3. **Transparency stack** (Ed 29:32–31:44): walk the entire tiered fee table out loud — "6% on the first $100,000… 5% from $100–250K… 1% above a million"; success fees keyed to milestones: "If we get you $40,000 funded, **you don't pay anything**. If we get you $50,000 plus, then it's a $3,000 admin success fee." And: "**This is all in writing, too.** I'll send you the agreement — I'm just going over it with you." Constantine's selective-transparency rule: "acknowledge minor cons first, then stack overwhelming pros" (7/15 debrief).
4. **Ask for MORE — never preemptively discount.** The $15K Jill close "was a direct result of challenging himself to ask for a higher upfront payment… managing objections rather than preemptively dropping the price" (7/15, fathom.video/calls/748651348). The drop-path exists but is a ladder you descend only under live objection: $8K → $6K → $4K → $2K, with backend percentage rising substantially as upfront falls so the top tier stays the client's best deal (7/1); flex to $0-upfront/higher-backend for qualified profiles (7/17, fathom.video/calls/751619158).
5. **Micro-commitment floor.** If finances genuinely block: a $300 deposit to start credit optimization kept Pradeep alive instead of dead (8/7, fathom.video/calls/775117204). A moving prospect beats a lost one.
Then: **silence.** (Doc: "value stack → price drop → silence.")
**Pre-handles:** Price (ROI math + guarantee), risk ("what if it doesn't work" — refund), skepticism (all in writing), and competitor shopping — vs a 10%-capped-at-$10K competitor, the counter is "motivation may drop after the cap is met; our guarantee is continued work at no cost until results" (Zacherly 7/31, fathom.video/calls/766265132).

# PART V — CLOSE

## Step 23 — Answer All + Assume the Sale
**Script (verbatim, Ed 31:53):** "So are you ready to get started, or do you have any questions?" → "No questions." → "Okay. You ready to get started?" → "**Let's do it.**" Language rules from coaching: "Ready to get the ball rolling?" beats "Is anything stopping you?"; "Does that make sense?" beats "Does that sound fair?" (7/17 + 8/5, fathom.video/calls/774323323).
**Pre-handles:** Nothing — by design. If Steps 1–22 ran, this step is administrative. Ed said yes to a fee structure with every number visible.

## Step 24 — Objections: Isolate + Solve (the four-category diagnostic)
**Purpose:** Route any stall to its real cause. Doc's categories: **1. Uncertainty** (fear/value/trust), **2. Finances** (don't have it / can't access it), **3. Partner** (no authority), **4. Timing & Logistics.**
**The elimination walk (verbatim, doc smokescreen section):** "It makes sense? You understand exactly how it works? Is this something that you want — do you want the funding? …In terms of logistics, you told me you can work through it, X amount of time weekly. You already tied in the partner. It sounds like the only potential piece left… is the actual fee itself." Then **call out the unspoken**: "Many prospects will never tell you to your face 'I don't think what you're charging is worth it' — literally 0% of the time — but it doesn't mean they're not thinking it. So you say: 'In terms of the finances — do you have the finances to invest in this? And do you see the value in what we're doing?'" For "I need to think about it": "Just so I can understand your thought process — what are some of the elements that you're considering?" Ask the same question two different ways; if the same answer comes back, **suggest** the likely objection yourself: "Let's go back to phase one — what questions do you have on phase one, or what clarity do you need there?" For vague objection-words: ask their definition first (8/5). Guarantee questions get the honest-mechanism answer (doc, verbatim): "I can't guarantee approval at any specific institution — I don't control their protocols. What I can say is we prepare your profile to be so underwriting-green-light compatible that it becomes very, very unreasonable to not succeed."
**Pre-handles:** Every category maps backward to a numbered step: Uncertainty→16–20, Finances→7+22, Partner→5, Timing→13. An objection here means a step was skipped — fix the step, not the symptom.

## Step 25 — Safety, Personal Guarantee, Agreement LAST
**Purpose:** The final emotion is safety (doc: reassurance, belonging, comfort — "leverage their emotional triggers, concern via genuine care").
**Script:** "My reputation is on the line. **I only deserve your money if I deliver value**" — frame the guarantee as personal integrity, not a contractual clause; and "present the agreement last, after all strategy and objections are resolved" (8/5 coaching, fathom.video/calls/774323323). Leo signed $12K on 8/8 after exactly this cycle (fathom.video/calls/777554648).
**Pre-handles:** "I don't trust guarantees" — answered emotionally, not contractually.

## Step 26 — The Pull-Back + Booked Next Step (never a dead end)
**Script:** When arguments are exhausted: "The decision is yours. Ball's in your court" — let them move toward you (8/5). For analytical stallers: don't press; project certainty and book a concrete 20-minute follow-up — "Thursday or Friday?" (8/5). Constantine's rationale (doc smokescreen, verbatim): "If they told you twice already 'I'm gonna have to circle back' — you just schedule the next meeting. Any more pushing makes it obvious you're trying to close them… weird vibes. Half a step before their guard comes up, pull back." Ed's same-day model: "Do you want to schedule a time?" → 5:15 booked before hanging up (Ed 32:34).
**Pre-handles:** The offer-without-next-step death: George got a custom offer and no recorded follow-up — dead (7/1, fathom.video/calls/730407363).

# THE OBJECTION PRE-HANDLE MAP

| Objection | Killed at Step | Kill mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Price / "too expensive" | 7, 8, 22 | Their own ROI number vs fee; refundable deposit + guarantee; ask-for-more then ladder |
| Spouse / partner | 5 (+ triage) | Reconfirmation before discovery; buy-in via partners' own goals |
| "I need to think about it" | 4, 20, 24, 26 | Definitive yes/no contract; temp-check surfaces doubts live; elimination walk; booked follow-up |
| Broker/lender expectation | 11 (+2) | Expectation check in triage/early discovery — the Ghani lesson |
| DIY ego / "I can do this myself" | 10, 12, 17 | Their own failed attempts on record; bucket self-selection; underwriting-nuance moat + unsell |
| Burned before / distrust | 3, 4, 15, 22, 25 | Metrics-based story; no-pressure frame; industry critique; everything in writing; personal-integrity guarantee |
| Competitor shopping | 22 | Motivation-after-cap risk + uncapped continued-work guarantee (Zacherly) |
| "Are you licensed?" | 3 | Track record vs paper certificate ($10M+ funded) |
| Can't afford it | 22.5 | Micro-commitment deposit ($300 Pradeep) or $0-up/higher-backend for qualified profiles |

# THE PRE-SOLD MECHANISM (summary)
The prospect sells themselves four times before hearing a price: **(1)** motivation stated in their own words (Step 2); **(2)** micro-agreement ladder — frame-yes (4), context-yes (3), permission-to-pitch-yes (15), per-stage "makes sense" yeses (17–19); **(3)** bucket self-selection (12); **(4)** temp-check self-sell (20). By the investment step the only person who has argued for the program is the prospect.

# THREE NAMED FAILURE MODES (from real losses)

**1. The Expert's Ego (Ghani, 7/15, lost).** 73-year-old ex-CPA, ex-lending-broker: "If a lender doesn't qualify me based on me, then I don't want that lender" / "I do not need coaching." Two compounding misses: psychological objection answered technically, and broker-expectation unqualified until minute 60. **Countermove:** run Step 11 early; at the first expert-identity signal, unsell ("you probably could do this yourself — the one thing I'd check is…"), reframe aged entity as SPV — "a standard, legal, technical tool" — and contrast their unworkable plan with the proven path; selective transparency (cons first, then pro-stack) (debrief, fathom.video/calls/748651348).

**2. The Preemptive Discount (Ed pricing postmortem, 7/1).** Ed closed at $2K — "a no-brainer for the client but a suboptimal outcome for the business" — because there was no structured ladder and price dropped before any objection existed. **Countermove:** open at the top tier; descend the 8/6/4/2 ladder only under live objection, with backend rising as upfront falls; the $15K Jill close is the proof the market pays when you ask (7/15).

**3. The Open Loop (George 7/1; Zacherly 7/31; P Reddy 8/10).** Offers left without a booked, dated next step die quietly: George never followed up; Zacherly left "deciding by Monday" against a cheaper capped competitor; P Reddy left at 7/10 to "do research." **Countermove:** no call ends without a calendared follow-up (Ed's same-day 5:15 booking is the standard); for shoppers, plant the motivation-after-cap risk + uncapped guarantee before they compare; for researchers, send proof material immediately and book the review call on the spot.
