# MASTER CLOSING FRAMEWORK — Grand Slam Sequence

Drafted 2026-08-10. Built exclusively from Constantine's written structure, the Alan+Constantine coaching sessions (Krisp), and real won/lost APW call recordings (Fathom). Every step cites its source. Companion doc: Closer Training — Sales Patterns & Playbook (Notion, 3b95bb1ffef48138a6e1cb3a0a90d880).

## How to read this
Constantine's architecture is **Intro/Frame → Discovery → Transition → Pitch → Close**. The design principle behind every step, in his words from the Sales Structure doc: Discovery exists to get "a) the information we need that is relevant to what we will pitch, b) reveal emotional leverage for the prospect to take action now, c) build rapport, and d) **eliminate objections before the close**." The close is not where objections are fought — it is where a properly-run call has already made them impossible. "One of the primary emotions that you need the prospect to feel → is **safety**: reassurance, belonging, comfort."

# PART I — INTRO / FRAME (2–5 min)

## Step 1 — Welcome + Location
**Purpose:** Human first contact; get them talking about something zero-stakes.
**Script (verbatim, Ghani call):** "So — where are you calling from?" …then relate genuinely ("Not too far away. I was in the Irvine area not too long ago.").
**Pre-handles:** Cold-formality / guardedness. A prospect who has answered two easy questions is already in answering rhythm before any sensitive question arrives.
**Source:** Sales Structure doc ("Welcome, location, source, why us"); Ghani 6:15 (fathom.video/calls/746607489).

## Step 2 — Source + Motivation (harvest self-sold data)
**Purpose:** Make the prospect state, in their own words, why they came. First plank of the pre-sold mechanism.
**Script:** "How did you end up finding us? Was it through an ad or a referral?" → "And what motivated you to reach out?" Then per the doc: "quick acknowledgement of what they said (**self sold data**) → transition to frame."
**Pre-handles:** "Why am I on this call?" and later think-about-it stalls — their stated motivation becomes callback ammunition for the pitch and close.
**Source:** Doc "Source" section; Ghani 6:47–7:29 ("you said you guarantee to find somebody… perfect fit" — his expectation surfaced in minute one; see Failure Mode 1).

## Step 3 — Permission-Based "Why Us" (credibility by metrics, not credentials)
**Purpose:** Establish authority through numbers before any pitch exists.
**Script (verbatim, Ghani 8:38–10:19):** "Before we get started, would it be helpful if I gave you a little bit of a background on the company as well as the agenda for the call?" → origin story: "I had a medical incident… it destroyed my credit… I ended up having a 500 credit score. And eventually, over time, I learned how to transform that 500 credit score to over 500K in funding… We've been in business since 2023… we've generated, using our systems, over $10 million in funding." Close the loop: "Was that context helpful, before we get started?"
Constantine's rule (6/17 session): "It's good, but it needs to be **tied to more metrics**… you want to talk about $500K plus in funding and growing… I've been doing this for X number of years… X number of clients and counting." And no name-dropping here — "detailed stories only if directly relevant… that's too much."
**Pre-handles:** "Are you certified/licensed?" — the answer is pre-loaded as track record vs paper ("contrast paper certificate vs track record, $10M+ funded," 7/15 coaching, fathom.video/calls/748467538). Also pre-handles burned-before: "helping many who have been routinely let down by the mass funding companies… that routinely over promise and under deliver" (doc, About Us).
**Source:** Doc "Clean" intro §4; Krisp 6/17; Ghani transcript.

## Step 4 — Strong Frame: pressure-off agenda + definitive yes-or-no contract
**Purpose:** Remove sales pressure AND contract for a decision — the single highest-leverage pre-handle in the system.
**Script (verbatim, doc):** "The purpose of this call is to walk through our process, to see if we are a good fit for one another, and to see if we can actually help you. If we can → we can discuss details later in the call. And if not → we will do our best to point you in the right direction — no big deal, and no hard feelings either way; we'll part ways as friends regardless… So all that I ask, is that by the end of the call, out of respect to both of us, you're able to give me a simple **definitive yes, or no**. Does that sound good to you?"
Live version that worked (Ghani 10:21): "…if we deem it's a good fit, we can discuss what it looks like moving forward. And if it's not, no big deal — either way, we'll point you in the right direction. Does that sound good?"
**Pre-handles:** (1) "I need to think about it" — they agreed up front to a yes/no; you can later invoke that agreement without being pushy. (2) Burned-before distrust — "for prospects burned by others, use a 'no pressure' frame to rebuild trust" (7/17 coaching, fathom.video/calls/751792038); this frame preceded the Leo $12K signature (8/8, fathom.video/calls/777554648).
**Source:** Doc "Strong frame"; Fathom 7/17.

## Step 5 — Partner Reconfirmation Checkpoint
**Purpose:** Confirm every decision-maker is present BEFORE investing 60 minutes.
**Script (verbatim, doc §5.5):** "Just before we get started, I wanted to confirm quickly… everyone is on the call that would be needed for financials, such as the PG, treasurer, partners, etc… just you? Or?"
Constantine's placement rule (6/10 session): partner qualification belongs in **triage**; the closing call gets only "a quick partner reconfirmation checkpoint at the start… before the Discovery/strong frame section" — "cold-opening with it risks triggering ego-defensive responses," so triage asks the low-friction "are your partners on the same page with funding?" inside the goals section.
**Pre-handles:** "I need to talk to my spouse/partner" — killed an hour before it could be said. Deeper version in discovery: "Who else would be involved? …Based on their roles → what are their goals? (get everyone's buy-in by speaking to **their** problems and goals)" (doc, Partner section).
**Source:** Doc §5.5 + Partner; Krisp 6/10.

# PART II — DISCOVERY (20–30 min)

## Step 6 — Main Challenge + Business Background
**Purpose:** Label their specific problem; understand the flow of money.
**Script (doc):** "If everything was perfect in your business right now, we wouldn't be speaking… so what is the main challenge or bottleneck in your business?" / "Tell me about your business — what do you do? How does it work? How does it operate?" If vague: "Aside from X, what else?" / "Can you expand on that?" / "What do you mean by that specifically?" Use **impact questions**: "when you see an opportunity to expose the impact of what they're telling you… ask a curious question so they can describe that specific impact."
**Frame it first** (6/3 session): "open the discovery by telling prospects that background questions will determine **whether funding is even the right path** — even if their credit qualifies." This "positions Alan as the decision-maker on fit, giving him authority and reducing resistance to non-credit questions."
**Pre-handles:** Value objections — a prospect who has described their own bottleneck in detail cannot later claim the problem isn't worth solving.
**Source:** Doc Discovery §1–2; Krisp 6/3.

## Step 7 — Money Block: amount, allocation, why funding
**Purpose:** Get the numbers the pitch will run on and the ROI the price will be compared against.
**Script:** "How much funding are you looking for?" → "How do you plan on investing that funding?" → "**Why** — how would it benefit you and change things for the better, specifically?" → "What would the funding allow you to do that you wouldn't be able to do without it — present and future?" (both sub-questions added in the 6/3 session). Pullback preframe (doc): "Not all companies require funding… so I just want to figure out if you actually do need funding… I want to make sure I'm recommending something you actually need."
**Pre-handles:** Price. When the use of funds is quantified (Ghani itemized ~$50K licensing + staff runway unprompted; Ashwini's $232K/yr interest, fathom.video/calls/764436554), the fee is later compared against their number, not against zero.
**Source:** Doc Money; Ghani 11:02–15:32.

## Step 8 — Runway Stretch (upsize the goal with a client-preframe)
**Purpose:** Expand the target — bigger goal, bigger urgency, bigger fee base.
**Script (verbatim, Ghani 15:48–18:11):** "Typically, a lot of the clients we work with, when they're budgeting for funding, they're not looking too far ahead… or factoring in the unknown variables… We suggest calculating at least six, if not 18 months worth of runway." → "How much funding would you need to secure to create six months of runway?" (Ghani: $150–200K became "$400K to be comfortable" in ninety seconds.) This is the doc's preframe pattern: "talk about other clients and what they would do → tie it back into a clarification question."
**Pre-handles:** "The amount you can get me isn't worth the fee" — they set the bigger number themselves.
**Source:** Ghani transcript; doc Background/preframe.

## Step 9 — Credit Qualification (with the three-fold rationale preframe)
**Purpose:** Qualify hard numbers; justify sensitive questions before asking them.
**Script (6/3 + doc):** "Now I'm going to shift into credit — the reason why is so we can know **if** we can actually fund you, **how much**, and **how fast**." Then: score per bureau; highest single-card limit ("10k plus preferred, 5k acceptable, 2500 bare minimum" — doc); 3–5 tradelines; 2+ years age; no delinquencies/derogs; utilization; inquiries per bureau; business age/standing/ownership. Live standard (Ed close): every number on the table — 767/788/788, 22+ accounts, >30% utilization being paid down, 7/8/1 inquiries, prior $80K stack, Chase/Amex blacklist.
**Pre-handles:** Post-sale surprises and guarantee disputes — the 7/1 pricing session flagged that "a deal was quoted before a full credit report review, revealing undisclosed issues post-sale." Secure the report pre-call (setter checklist step 10, doc; 7/22 session: the ask is reframed as an act of helping — "without it, prospects can't get funded by anyone").
**Source:** Doc Qualification; Krisp 6/3 + 7/22; Ed transcript (fathom.video/calls/728895030).

## Step 10 — Efforts + How Long (stretch pain; mine their failures)
**Purpose:** Surface what they've tried, so the pitch is positioned against their own lived failures.
**Script:** "Have you ever tried to get funding in the past?" (the 6/3 bridge question from credit → efforts). Follow the Ed pattern (12:09–16:26): "Did you work with a company or do it yourself?" → "Why didn't you continue with them?" → "Then you tried on your own — what were the results?" → Ed: "**It was a disaster. No success at all.**"
**Pre-handles:** DIY-ego AND burned-before, simultaneously. Ed convicted himself: company got him $80K but only once; solo attempt failed. The pitch then only had to be "the thing that fixes what you already told me failed." Constantine's unsell backup for know-it-alls: "agree they probably could, then expose one flaw in their logic for the aha moment" (7/15, fathom.video/calls/748467538).
**Source:** Doc Efforts/How long; Ed transcript; Fathom 7/15.

## Step 11 — Expectation Check (the Ghani question)
**Purpose:** Confirm they understand WHAT we are — coaching/consulting with lender access — before an hour is invested.
**Script (built from the loss):** "Just so I set expectations properly — some people come to us expecting a licensed loan broker they can hand a package to. What we actually are is [coaching/consulting + lender database + done-for-you execution]. Which were you picturing?"
**Pre-handles:** The broker-expectation mismatch that killed Ghani at minute 60: "I thought that you have a pool of lenders… and you are a broker… I was going to delegate that task to you. But if… you are not endorsed with NMLS… **then I will pass on your services**" (1:07–1:08). Constantine's debrief: qualify urgency/authority/ability in the first 5 minutes (fathom.video/calls/739886841); this check should have run in triage (debrief, fathom.video/calls/748651348).
**Source:** Ghani transcript; 7/15 debrief.

## Step 12 — Bucket Discernment (prospect self-selects the offer)
**Purpose:** Have them choose their own delivery model — second plank of the pre-sold mechanism.
**Script (verbatim, Ghani 41:39–43:08):** "We have three buckets people typically fall in. Bucket one: 'I just want to do this myself — teach me.' Bucket two: 'I don't have time, I want you to do it for me.' Bucket three: hybrid — 'do it for me in the beginning, teach me along the way so I can fund myself forever.' Out of those three, which would you say you align with most?" Ed's version, assumptive (28:22): "Normally we have a program where we teach people how to do this themselves… but obviously you're super busy, so that doesn't sound like it would be for you, correct?" — "Correct."
**Pre-handles:** "I could do this myself." Whoever picks bucket 2/3 has conceded they want it done for them. **Danger signal:** bucket 1 + expert self-identity (Ghani: "I do not need coaching") = the Expert's Ego failure mode; pivot immediately to Step 26's countermove. Strategy note (6/17): pitch DFY as primary ("give them what the market wants"), training delivered at the end as differentiator — "the last thing we want them to leave the call with is the idea that they can look into this and do it on their own." Two competitive edges (6/10): no 10% funding fee (vs competitors' $10K–$25K+ on $100–250K deals) and future independence.
**Source:** Ghani + Ed transcripts; Krisp 6/17 + 6/10.

## Step 13 — Timing, Logistics & Commitment (future-pace + micro-agreement)
**Purpose:** Lock time commitment and "why now" before price exists.
**Script (doc):** "Do you feel like NOW is the right time — why now vs later?" "Is there anything that would get in the way of this — projects, vacations?" → "In terms of our most successful clients, they're able to tie in roughly 30–60 minutes per day on average consistently… Is this something you can realistically commit to?" Timing resistance → "Walk me through a typical day — you wake up at what time? …" Mindset preframe: "Our most successful clients understand the right mindset in how to interpret problems — and that's exactly what we teach. So what that means is, when XYZ inevitably happens, we coach you how to properly navigate those challenges so you don't get frustrated hitting walls."
**Pre-handles:** "Now's not the right time" and logistics smokescreens — both answered on record 30 minutes before the close (see Step 24's elimination walk).
**Source:** Doc Timing/Logistics/Commitment.

## Step 14 — Prompt for Missed Info
**Purpose:** Close discovery airtight.
**Script (doc):** "Is there anything else that I need to know about your business or background, in order to make the best recommendation for you?"
**Pre-handles:** Late-surfacing facts ("oh, by the way, I have a bankruptcy…") that would otherwise detonate in the close.
**Source:** Doc.

# PART III — TRANSITION

## Step 15 — Summary → Certainty Statement → Permission to Pitch
**Purpose:** Convert discovery into a fit-verdict, then get invited to pitch.
**Script (doc):** Summarize ("Accurate? What else do you want to add?") → "Based on everything that you've told me, **you fit the profile of our most successful clients**. So that being the case, I want to share our process with you from A-Z. Are you ready for me to go ahead with that?" The certainty statement is the industry critique: "I've personally gone through 100+ ads and offers from the leading companies… What I learned was: 1) it is WAY too common for these companies to OVER-promise and UNDER-deliver, 2) the marketing number is often not realistic (this is why we state a range vs a fixed amount), 3) the salespeople typically are NOT experienced in funding themselves — they sell the concept without first-hand knowledge of what gets people approved and denied in underwriting."
**Pre-handles:** Burned-before (we name the exact way they got burned, and structurally differ) and resistance-to-pitch (they said "yes, go ahead" — micro-agreement #3 of the ladder: frame-yes at Step 4, buckets at Step 12, permission here).
**Source:** Doc Transition.

# PART IV — PITCH (5–10 min)

## Step 16 — Preface: Outcome + Social Proof → "through this 3-stage process"
**Purpose:** Anchor the goal number, re-anchor credibility, open the staged walkthrough.
**Script (verbatim, doc Pitch Updated + 6/17 mock):** "So the goal is for us to secure ___ in funding. Now, the way we've done that for our clients — [500 → $500K+ personal; industry since 2023; $10M+ client funding] — is through a three-stage process…" Slides: max 1–2 per stage, bullets only — "you do most of the explaining… if following along becomes inundation, they feel overwhelmed" (Constantine, 6/17).
**Pre-handles:** Uncertainty/trust — the #1 close-killer in Constantine's four-category model.
**Source:** Doc; Krisp 6/17.

## Step 17 — Stage 1 Credit Optimization: Callback → Solution → Benefit → Prompt
**Purpose:** First proof of expertise, customized with their own numbers.
**Script:** Callback (6/17 mock): "So earlier you told me you have a 750 credit score, more than three cards, your highest limit is at least $10K — you have a strong profile…" Solution: names/addresses/employers cleanup, inquiry removal, utilization to 1–7% ("the mere fact that I'm referring back to what you told me in discovery makes the thing feel like it's more for me" — Constantine, 6/17). Benefit (doc, verbatim): "→ **OPTIMIZED FOR FUNDING — AUTOMATED HIGH-LIMIT APPROVALS**, instead of low limits, long delays, and denials." The silver-platter frame that landed live: "we're bringing them your credit report on a golden silver platter" → Ghani himself completed it: "**So they have every reason to say yes, no reason to say no**" (32:42). Prompt: "So that's stage one. What questions do you have on that specifically?" / "How are you feeling so far?"
**Pre-handles:** DIY-ego (underwriting nuance = expertise moat) and "why do you need all this" — every deliverable is tied to a fact they gave you.
**Source:** Doc Pitch Updated; Krisp 6/17; Ghani + Ed transcripts.

## Step 18 — Stage 2 Funding Strategy & Approvals → Prompt
**Script:** "Then we build your **customized funding sequence** — specific to your geolocation and your specific profile — exactly where we're going to go, what we're going to say, what we're going to do" (Ghani 39:20: "capital sequencing plan"). Differentiation data point: "ASCEND's 12,000+ data-point database to target institutions" (P Reddy 8/10, fathom.video/calls/777298604). Prompt for questions again.
**Pre-handles:** "What am I actually paying for?" — the strategy layer is the thing DIY can't replicate (Step 10's admission).

## Step 19 — Stage 3 Execution & Advanced Strategies → Wrap
**Script:** "The final stage is the one everyone loves — the approvals. We're working advanced strategies and compounding results to your $___ goal, and eventually $___" (Ghani 40:06). Wrap: "math"/outcome + confidence social-proof statement (doc). Ed's live wrap (27:35): "So from what you understand about us taking you through credit optimization, to the custom strategy specifically for you and your geolocation, to the funding itself, with inquiry removal throughout — what questions do you have about any of those steps?"
**Pre-handles:** Process uncertainty — three prompts across three stages means no doubt survives to the close unspoken.

## Step 20 — Temp Check 1–10: the prospect self-sells
**Purpose:** The keystone of the pre-sold mechanism — they argue FOR the program.
**Script (verbatim, doc):** "How are you feeling on the whole process, on a scale of 1–10?" **If 8+:** "That's great — what do you feel would be especially beneficial or helpful?" **If below 8:** "What would make you a 10?" ("you have to get their certainty up… you need them to tell you, and sell themselves on why.")
**Pre-handles:** "I need to think about it" — the thinking happens here, out loud, with you in the room. **Signal discipline:** Ghani deflected the temp check ("Words are not an indicative of performance… I'm 100% okay with everything you said" — 50:58) and refused testimonials; an evasive temp-check answer means certainty is NOT built — loop back, do not proceed to price. P Reddy answered "7/10" and stalled into "I need to research you" (8/10) — the 7 was the tell; "what would make you a 10" is mandatory, not optional.
**Source:** Doc Rank-on-Scale; Ghani + P Reddy calls.

## Step 21 — Next Steps / Future Pace (x → y → z)
**Script (verbatim, Ed 32:06):** "The process after this is: we get the agreement signed, we do the payment, and then we get you into onboarding — it'll just run you through a bunch of really easy videos." Doc: 10–15 seconds, "day 0 → onboarding… day X this… day B…"
**Pre-handles:** Fear of the unknown post-yes. Saying yes now has a picture attached.

## Step 22 — Investment: the Grand Slam Offer Assembly
**Purpose:** Present price as a de-risked, ROI-positive, transparent structure. Order (doc): **value stack → ROI → price drop → silence.**
**The five components, all field-proven:**
1. **Refundable deposit + funding guarantee** (Ed 29:10, verbatim): "It's just $2,000 up front… which is refundable if $20,000 minimum in funding is not secured — which would be a 10x return… Does that make sense so far?" Engineered deliberately on 7/1 (fathom.video/calls/731966182): "full refund guarantee to de-risk the offer." Current calibration: $5K deposit / $50K floor (P Reddy).
2. **Best case / worst case framing** (7/1): "Best case: you invest upfront, receive significant funding, the fee becomes irrelevant. Worst case: full refund, **plus** a detailed explanation of why funding failed to guide your next move." Either way they win — the no-lose geometry.
3. **Transparency stack** (Ed 29:32–31:44): walk the entire tiered fee table out loud — "6% on the first $100,000… 5% from $100–250K… 1% above a million"; success fees keyed to milestones: "If we get you $40,000 funded, **you don't pay anything**. If we get you $50,000 plus, then it's a $3,000 admin success fee." And: "**This is all in writing, too.** I'll send you the agreement — I'm just going over it with you." Constantine's selective-transparency rule: "acknowledge minor cons first, then stack overwhelming pros" (7/15 debrief).
4. **Ask for MORE — never preemptively discount.** The $15K Jill close "was a direct result of challenging himself to ask for a higher upfront payment… managing objections rather than preemptively dropping the price" (7/15, fathom.video/calls/748651348). The drop-path exists but is a ladder you descend only under live objection: $8K → $6K → $4K → $2K, with backend percentage rising substantially as upfront falls so the top tier stays the client's best deal (7/1); flex to $0-upfront/higher-backend for qualified profiles (7/17, fathom.video/calls/751619158).
5. **Micro-commitment floor.** If finances genuinely block: a $300 deposit to start credit optimization kept Pradeep alive instead of dead (8/7, fathom.video/calls/775117204). A moving prospect beats a lost one.
Then: **silence.** (Doc: "value stack → price drop → silence.")
**Pre-handles:** Price (ROI math + guarantee), risk ("what if it doesn't work" — refund), skepticism (all in writing), and competitor shopping — vs a 10%-capped-at-$10K competitor, the counter is "motivation may drop after the cap is met; our guarantee is continued work at no cost until results" (Zacherly 7/31, fathom.video/calls/766265132).

# PART V — CLOSE

## Step 23 — Answer All + Assume the Sale
**Script (verbatim, Ed 31:53):** "So are you ready to get started, or do you have any questions?" → "No questions." → "Okay. You ready to get started?" → "**Let's do it.**" Language rules from coaching: "Ready to get the ball rolling?" beats "Is anything stopping you?"; "Does that make sense?" beats "Does that sound fair?" (7/17 + 8/5, fathom.video/calls/774323323).
**Pre-handles:** Nothing — by design. If Steps 1–22 ran, this step is administrative. Ed said yes to a fee structure with every number visible.

## Step 24 — Objections: Isolate + Solve (the four-category diagnostic)
**Purpose:** Route any stall to its real cause. Doc's categories: **1. Uncertainty** (fear/value/trust), **2. Finances** (don't have it / can't access it), **3. Partner** (no authority), **4. Timing & Logistics.**
**The elimination walk (verbatim, doc smokescreen section):** "It makes sense? You understand exactly how it works? Is this something that you want — do you want the funding? …In terms of logistics, you told me you can work through it, X amount of time weekly. You already tied in the partner. It sounds like the only potential piece left… is the actual fee itself." Then **call out the unspoken**: "Many prospects will never tell you to your face 'I don't think what you're charging is worth it' — literally 0% of the time — but it doesn't mean they're not thinking it. So you say: 'In terms of the finances — do you have the finances to invest in this? And do you see the value in what we're doing?'" For "I need to think about it": "Just so I can understand your thought process — what are some of the elements that you're considering?" Ask the same question two different ways; if the same answer comes back, **suggest** the likely objection yourself: "Let's go back to phase one — what questions do you have on phase one, or what clarity do you need there?" For vague objection-words: ask their definition first (8/5). Guarantee questions get the honest-mechanism answer (doc, verbatim): "I can't guarantee approval at any specific institution — I don't control their protocols. What I can say is we prepare your profile to be so underwriting-green-light compatible that it becomes very, very unreasonable to not succeed."
**Pre-handles:** Every category maps backward to a numbered step: Uncertainty→16–20, Finances→7+22, Partner→5, Timing→13. An objection here means a step was skipped — fix the step, not the symptom.

## Step 25 — Safety, Personal Guarantee, Agreement LAST
**Purpose:** The final emotion is safety (doc: reassurance, belonging, comfort — "leverage their emotional triggers, concern via genuine care").
**Script:** "My reputation is on the line. **I only deserve your money if I deliver value**" — frame the guarantee as personal integrity, not a contractual clause; and "present the agreement last, after all strategy and objections are resolved" (8/5 coaching, fathom.video/calls/774323323). Leo signed $12K on 8/8 after exactly this cycle (fathom.video/calls/777554648).
**Pre-handles:** "I don't trust guarantees" — answered emotionally, not contractually.

## Step 26 — The Pull-Back + Booked Next Step (never a dead end)
**Script:** When arguments are exhausted: "The decision is yours. Ball's in your court" — let them move toward you (8/5). For analytical stallers: don't press; project certainty and book a concrete 20-minute follow-up — "Thursday or Friday?" (8/5). Constantine's rationale (doc smokescreen, verbatim): "If they told you twice already 'I'm gonna have to circle back' — you just schedule the next meeting. Any more pushing makes it obvious you're trying to close them… weird vibes. Half a step before their guard comes up, pull back." Ed's same-day model: "Do you want to schedule a time?" → 5:15 booked before hanging up (Ed 32:34).
**Pre-handles:** The offer-without-next-step death: George got a custom offer and no recorded follow-up — dead (7/1, fathom.video/calls/730407363).

# THE OBJECTION PRE-HANDLE MAP

| Objection | Killed at Step | Kill mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Price / "too expensive" | 7, 8, 22 | Their own ROI number vs fee; refundable deposit + guarantee; ask-for-more then ladder |
| Spouse / partner | 5 (+ triage) | Reconfirmation before discovery; buy-in via partners' own goals |
| "I need to think about it" | 4, 20, 24, 26 | Definitive yes/no contract; temp-check surfaces doubts live; elimination walk; booked follow-up |
| Broker/lender expectation | 11 (+2) | Expectation check in triage/early discovery — the Ghani lesson |
| DIY ego / "I can do this myself" | 10, 12, 17 | Their own failed attempts on record; bucket self-selection; underwriting-nuance moat + unsell |
| Burned before / distrust | 3, 4, 15, 22, 25 | Metrics-based story; no-pressure frame; industry critique; everything in writing; personal-integrity guarantee |
| Competitor shopping | 22 | Motivation-after-cap risk + uncapped continued-work guarantee (Zacherly) |
| "Are you licensed?" | 3 | Track record vs paper certificate ($10M+ funded) |
| Can't afford it | 22.5 | Micro-commitment deposit ($300 Pradeep) or $0-up/higher-backend for qualified profiles |

# THE PRE-SOLD MECHANISM (summary)
The prospect sells themselves four times before hearing a price: **(1)** motivation stated in their own words (Step 2); **(2)** micro-agreement ladder — frame-yes (4), context-yes (3), permission-to-pitch-yes (15), per-stage "makes sense" yeses (17–19); **(3)** bucket self-selection (12); **(4)** temp-check self-sell (20). By the investment step the only person who has argued for the program is the prospect.

# THREE NAMED FAILURE MODES (from real losses)

**1. The Expert's Ego (Ghani, 7/15, lost).** 73-year-old ex-CPA, ex-lending-broker: "If a lender doesn't qualify me based on me, then I don't want that lender" / "I do not need coaching." Two compounding misses: psychological objection answered technically, and broker-expectation unqualified until minute 60. **Countermove:** run Step 11 early; at the first expert-identity signal, unsell ("you probably could do this yourself — the one thing I'd check is…"), reframe aged entity as SPV — "a standard, legal, technical tool" — and contrast their unworkable plan with the proven path; selective transparency (cons first, then pro-stack) (debrief, fathom.video/calls/748651348).

**2. The Preemptive Discount (Ed pricing postmortem, 7/1).** Ed closed at $2K — "a no-brainer for the client but a suboptimal outcome for the business" — because there was no structured ladder and price dropped before any objection existed. **Countermove:** open at the top tier; descend the 8/6/4/2 ladder only under live objection, with backend rising as upfront falls; the $15K Jill close is the proof the market pays when you ask (7/15).

**3. The Open Loop (George 7/1; Zacherly 7/31; P Reddy 8/10).** Offers left without a booked, dated next step die quietly: George never followed up; Zacherly left "deciding by Monday" against a cheaper capped competitor; P Reddy left at 7/10 to "do research." **Countermove:** no call ends without a calendared follow-up (Ed's same-day 5:15 booking is the standard); for shoppers, plant the motivation-after-cap risk + uncapped guarantee before they compare; for researchers, send proof material immediately and book the review call on the spot.

MASTER CLOSING FRAMEWORK — Grand Slam Sequence (Ascend Prime Wealth closer training)

Built exclusively from Constantine's written Sales Structure, the Alan+Constantine coaching sessions, and real won/lost APW call recordings. Architecture: Intro/Frame → Discovery → Transition → Pitch → Close. Design principle: Discovery exists to get "the information we need that is relevant to what we will pitch, reveal emotional leverage for the prospect to take action now, build rapport, and eliminate objections before the close." The close is not where objections are fought — a properly-run call has already made them impossible. The primary emotion the prospect must feel: SAFETY (reassurance, belonging, comfort).

PART I — INTRO / FRAME (2–5 min)

Step 1 — Welcome + Location. Purpose: human first contact; get them talking about something zero-stakes. Script: "So — where are you calling from?" then relate genuinely. Pre-handles: cold-formality/guardedness — a prospect who has answered two easy questions is in answering rhythm before any sensitive question arrives.

Step 2 — Source + Motivation (harvest self-sold data). Purpose: make the prospect state, in their own words, why they came — first plank of the pre-sold mechanism. Script: "How did you end up finding us — an ad or a referral?" → "What motivated you to reach out?" → quick acknowledgement (SELF SOLD DATA) → transition to frame. Pre-handles: "why am I on this call" and later think-about-it stalls — their stated motivation becomes callback ammunition.

Step 3 — Permission-Based "Why Us" (credibility by metrics, not credentials). Script: "Before we get started, would it be helpful if I gave you a little background on the company and the agenda for the call?" → origin story: "I had a medical incident… it destroyed my credit… I had a 500 credit score. Over time I learned how to transform that 500 score into over $500K in funding… in business since 2023… over $10 million in client funding." Close the loop: "Was that context helpful?" Rule: tie to metrics ($500K+ personal, $10M+ clients, years, client count) — no name-dropping, no long stories. Pre-handles: "Are you certified/licensed?" (track record vs paper certificate) and burned-before ("helping people routinely let down by mass funding companies that over-promise and under-deliver").

Step 4 — Strong Frame: pressure-off agenda + definitive yes-or-no contract. THE single highest-leverage pre-handle. Script: "The purpose of this call is to walk through our process, see if we're a good fit, and see if we can actually help you. If we can — we'll discuss details later in the call. If not — we'll point you in the right direction, no big deal, no hard feelings, we part as friends either way. All I ask is that by the end of the call, out of respect to both of us, you give me a simple definitive yes or no. Does that sound good?" Pre-handles: "I need to think about it" (they contracted to a decision) and burned-before distrust (pressure-off frame rebuilds trust — this preceded the $12K Leo signature).

Step 5 — Partner Reconfirmation Checkpoint. Script: "Before we get started — is everyone on the call that would be needed for financials: PG, treasurer, partners? Just you, or?" Placement: full partner qualification belongs in triage; the closing call gets a quick reconfirmation only (cold-opening risks ego-defensive responses). Pre-handles: "I need to talk to my spouse/partner" — killed an hour before it could be said.

PART II — DISCOVERY (20–30 min)

Step 6 — Main Challenge + Business Background. Script: "If everything was perfect in your business we wouldn't be speaking — what's the main challenge or bottleneck?" / "Tell me about your business — how does it operate?" Drill: "Aside from X, what else?" "What do you mean by that specifically?" Use impact questions to expose the cost of the problem. Frame first: background questions determine whether funding is even the right path — positions the closer as the decision-maker on fit. Pre-handles: value objections — they described their own bottleneck.

Step 7 — Money Block: amount, allocation, why. Script: "How much funding are you looking for?" → "How do you plan on investing it?" → "Why — how would it change things, specifically?" → "What would funding let you do that you couldn't do without it — now and in the future?" Pullback preframe: "Not all companies require funding… I want to make sure I'm recommending something you actually need." Pre-handles: price — the fee is later compared against THEIR quantified ROI number, not against zero.

Step 8 — Runway Stretch (upsize the goal). Script: "Most clients budgeting for funding aren't looking far enough ahead or factoring the unknowns. We suggest calculating at least 6, if not 18 months of runway. How much would you need for six months of runway?" (Real result: a $150–200K ask became "$400K to be comfortable" in ninety seconds.) Pre-handles: "the amount isn't worth the fee" — they set the bigger number themselves.

Step 9 — Credit Qualification with three-fold rationale. Script: "Now I'm going to shift into credit — so we can know IF we can fund you, HOW MUCH, and HOW FAST." Then: scores per bureau, highest card limit (10K+ preferred, 5K acceptable, 2.5K bare minimum), 3–5 tradelines, 2+ years age, delinquencies, utilization, inquiries per bureau, business age/standing. Standard: every number on the table before pricing. Pre-handles: post-sale surprises and guarantee disputes (never quote before the full report).

Step 10 — Efforts + How Long (mine their failures). Script: "Have you tried to get funding before?" → "With a company or yourself?" → "Why didn't you continue with them?" → "What were the results on your own?" (Real answer that closed $2K same-day: "It was a disaster. No success at all.") Pre-handles: DIY-ego and burned-before simultaneously — the pitch becomes "the fix for what you told me failed."

Step 11 — Expectation Check. Script: "So I set expectations properly — some people expect a licensed loan broker they hand a package to. What we actually are is coaching/consulting plus lender database plus done-for-you execution. Which were you picturing?" Pre-handles: the broker-expectation mismatch that killed a 60-minute call at the close ("if you are not endorsed with NMLS, I will pass").

Step 12 — Bucket Discernment (prospect self-selects). Script: "Three buckets: 1) teach me, I'll do it myself. 2) I don't have time — do it for me. 3) Hybrid — do it for me while teaching me so I can fund myself forever. Which do you align with most?" Assumptive variant: "Normally we teach people to do this themselves — but you're super busy, so that doesn't sound like it's for you, correct?" Pre-handles: "I could do this myself." Danger signal: bucket 1 + expert identity = Expert's Ego failure mode — pivot to unsell. Strategy: pitch done-for-you as primary; independence as the differentiator; competitive edges = no 10% funding fee and future independence.

Step 13 — Timing, Logistics & Commitment. Script: "Do you feel NOW is the right time — why now vs later?" "Anything that would get in the way — projects, vacations?" "Our most successful clients tie in 30–60 minutes per day. Can you realistically commit to that?" Mindset preframe: "when challenges inevitably happen, we coach you through them so you don't get frustrated hitting walls." Pre-handles: "now's not the right time" and logistics smokescreens — answered on record 30 minutes before the close.

Step 14 — Prompt for Missed Info. "Anything else I need to know to make the best recommendation for you?" Pre-handles late-surfacing facts that would detonate in the close.

PART III — TRANSITION

Step 15 — Summary → Certainty Statement → Permission to Pitch. Summarize ("Accurate? Anything to add?") → "Based on everything you've told me, you fit the profile of our most successful clients. I want to share our process A-Z. Ready for me to go ahead?" Certainty statement (industry critique): "I've gone through 100+ ads and offers from the leading companies. What I learned: they over-promise and under-deliver; the marketing number is often unrealistic (that's why we state a range); and their salespeople have usually never funded themselves — they sell a concept without knowing what passes underwriting." Pre-handles: burned-before (names exactly how they got burned) and resistance-to-pitch (they invited it — third yes of the micro-agreement ladder).

PART IV — PITCH (5–10 min)

Step 16 — Preface: outcome + social proof → "through this 3-stage process." "The goal is to secure $___ in funding. The way we've done that — 500 score to $500K personally, $10M+ for clients since 2023 — is through a three-stage process." Slides: 1–2 per stage, bullets only; the closer does the explaining.

Step 17 — Stage 1: Credit Optimization. Callback → Solution → Benefit → Prompt. Callback their exact numbers ("you told me you have a 750 score, 3+ cards, $10K+ top limit — strong profile"). Solution: cleanup, inquiry removal, utilization to 1–7%. Benefit: "OPTIMIZED FOR FUNDING — AUTOMATED HIGH-LIMIT APPROVALS instead of low limits, delays, and denials." The winning frame: "we bring the banks your credit report on a silver platter — they have every reason to say yes, no reason to say no." Prompt: "What questions do you have on that specifically?"

Step 18 — Stage 2: Funding Strategy & Approvals. "We build your customized funding sequence — specific to your geolocation and profile: exactly where we go, what we say, what we do" — powered by a 12,000+ data-point institution database. Prompt again. Pre-handles "what am I paying for": strategy is the moat DIY can't replicate.

Step 19 — Stage 3: Execution & Advanced Strategies. "The stage everyone loves — the approvals. Advanced strategies compounding to your $___ goal and beyond." Wrap with the full-arc question: "From credit optimization, to the custom strategy for your geolocation, to the funding itself — what questions on any of those steps?"

Step 20 — Temp Check 1–10: the prospect self-sells. "How are you feeling about the whole process, 1–10?" If 8+: "Great — what do you feel would be especially beneficial?" If below 8: "What would make you a 10?" They must tell you and sell themselves. Signal discipline: an evasive or deflected answer ("I'm 100% okay with everything you said") means certainty is NOT built — loop back, do not proceed to price. A "7" that isn't cured becomes "I need to do research."

Step 21 — Next Steps / Future Pace. 10–15 seconds: "We sign the agreement, take payment, and get you into onboarding — easy videos, day-by-day." Pre-handles fear of the unknown after yes.

Step 22 — Investment: the Grand Slam Offer Assembly. Order: VALUE STACK → ROI → PRICE DROP → SILENCE. Five components: (1) Refundable deposit + funding guarantee: "$2,000 upfront — refundable if $20,000 minimum in funding is not secured — a 10x return. Make sense so far?" (current calibration $5K deposit / $50K floor). (2) Best case / worst case: "Best case — you get significant funding and the fee becomes irrelevant. Worst case — full refund PLUS a detailed explanation of why funding failed. Either way you win." (3) Transparency stack: walk the whole tiered fee table out loud — 6% first $100K, 5% to $250K, down to 1% above $1M; success fees keyed to milestones ("under $40K funded you pay nothing") — "and this is all in writing; I'll send you the agreement." Acknowledge minor cons first, then stack the pros. (4) Ask for MORE — never preemptively discount. The $15K close came from asking higher and managing objections; the ladder ($8K → $6K → $4K → $2K, backend rising as upfront falls) exists only for live objections. (5) Micro-commitment floor: a $300 deposit to start credit optimization keeps a money-tight deal alive. Then: silence.

PART V — CLOSE

Step 23 — Answer All + Assume the Sale. "So are you ready to get started, or do you have any questions?" → "Ready to get the ball rolling?" (never "Is anything stopping you?"). If steps 1–22 ran, this step is administrative — the real close already happened.

Step 24 — Objections: Isolate + Solve, four-category diagnostic: Uncertainty / Finances / Partner / Timing-Logistics. The elimination walk: "It makes sense? You understand how it works? You want the funding? Logistics — you told me you can commit the time. Partner's on board. So the only piece left… is the fee itself." Call out the unspoken: "Prospects will never say 'I don't think it's worth it' to your face — 0% of the time — but they think it. So ask: do you have the finances to invest, and do you see the value?" For "think about it": "Walk me through your thought process — what elements are you considering?" Same answer twice → suggest the objection yourself and re-open the relevant stage. Guarantee questions get the honest mechanism: "I can't guarantee approval at any specific institution — I don't control their protocols. What I can say is we prepare your profile to be so underwriting-green-light compatible that it becomes very, very unreasonable not to succeed." Every objection maps to a numbered step: Uncertainty→16–20, Finances→7+22, Partner→5, Timing→13. An objection means a step was skipped — fix the step, not the symptom.

Step 25 — Safety, Personal Guarantee, Agreement LAST. "My reputation is on the line. I only deserve your money if I deliver value." Frame the guarantee as personal integrity; present the agreement last, after all strategy and objections are resolved. This exact cycle closed the $12K signature.

Step 26 — The Pull-Back + Booked Next Step (never a dead end). When arguments are exhausted: "The decision is yours — ball's in your court." Analytical stallers: don't press; project certainty and book a concrete 20-minute follow-up — "Thursday or Friday?" Rationale: "If they've told you twice they'll circle back, schedule the meeting — more pushing makes it obvious you're closing them. Half a step before their guard comes up, pull back." Standard: no call ends without a calendared next step (the winning model booked same-day 5:15 before hanging up).

THE OBJECTION PRE-HANDLE MAP
Price → Steps 7, 8, 22 (their ROI number vs fee; refundable guarantee; ask-more-then-ladder). Spouse/partner → Step 5 + triage. "Think about it" → Steps 4, 20, 24, 26. Broker/lender expectation → Step 11. DIY ego → Steps 10, 12, 17. Burned before → Steps 3, 4, 15, 22, 25. Competitor shopping → Step 22 (motivation-drops-after-cap risk + uncapped continued-work guarantee). "Are you licensed?" → Step 3 (track record vs paper). Can't afford → Step 22.5 (micro-deposit or $0-up/higher-backend for qualified profiles).

THE PRE-SOLD MECHANISM
The prospect sells themselves four times before hearing a price: (1) motivation in their own words (Step 2); (2) the micro-agreement ladder — frame-yes, context-yes, permission-to-pitch-yes, per-stage "makes sense" yeses; (3) bucket self-selection (Step 12); (4) the 1–10 temp-check self-sell (Step 20). By the investment step, the only person who has argued for the program is the prospect.

THREE NAMED FAILURE MODES (from real losses)
1. The Expert's Ego: ex-broker prospect — "I do not need coaching." Psychological objection answered technically + expectation unqualified until minute 60. Countermove: run Step 11 early; unsell ("you probably could do this yourself — the one thing I'd check is…"); reframe aged entity as a standard legal SPV tool; cons first, then pro-stack.
2. The Preemptive Discount: a close at $2K that should have been more — price dropped before any objection existed. Countermove: open at the top tier; descend the ladder only under live objection; the $15K close proves the market pays when you ask.
3. The Open Loop: offers left without a booked, dated next step die quietly (three real examples: no follow-up ever, "deciding by Monday" against a cheaper competitor, "7/10, I'll do research"). Countermove: calendar the follow-up before hanging up, every time; plant the competitor counter before they compare; send proof material immediately and book the review call on the spot.

**Step 3 — Permission-Based "Why Us" (metrics, not credentials).** "Before we start, would it be helpful if I gave you background on the company and the agenda?" → origin story: 500 score → $500K+ personal funding; in business since 2023; $10M+ generated for clients. **Step 4 — Strong Frame: pressure-off agenda + definitive yes/no contract.** THE highest-leverage pre-handle: "The purpose of this call is to walk through our process, see if we're a good fit, and see if we can actually help you. If we can — we discuss details later in the call. If not — we point you in the right direction, no big deal, no hard feelings, we part as friends. All I ask is that by the end, out of respect to both of us, you give me a simple **definitive yes or no**. Sound good?" *Pre-handles "I need to think about it" + rebuilds trust with burned prospects (preceded the $12K Leo signature).*

**Step 5 — Partner Reconfirmation Checkpoint.** "Before we start — is everyone on who'd be needed for financials: PG, treasurer, partners? Just you, or?" (Full partner qualification lives in triage; this is a 10-second reconfirm.) *Kills "I need to talk to my spouse/partner" an hour before it could be said.*

Pullback preframe: "Not everyone needs funding… I want to recommend what you actually need." *The fee is later compared against THEIR ROI number, not zero.*

**Step 8 — Runway Stretch.** "Most clients don't budget far enough ahead. We suggest 6–18 months of runway — how much would six months take?" (Real result: $150–200K became "$400K to be comfortable" in 90 seconds.) *They upsize their own goal.*

**Step 9 — Credit Qualification (three-fold rationale).** "Now I'll shift into credit — so we know IF we can fund you, HOW MUCH, and HOW FAST." Scores per bureau, top limit (10K+ preferred / 5K ok / 2.5K minimum), tradelines, age, derogs, utilization, inquiries, business age. Every number on the table before pricing. *Never quote before the full report — prevents post-sale surprises and guarantee disputes.*

**Step 10 — Efforts + How Long (mine their failures).** "Tried getting funding before? With a company or yourself? Why didn't you continue? What were your solo results?" (The $2K same-day close answered: "It was a disaster. No success at all.") *Kills DIY-ego and burned-before at once — the pitch fixes what THEY said failed.*

**Step 11 — Expectation Check (the Ghani question).** "So I set expectations properly — some people expect a licensed broker they hand a package to. What we actually are is coaching/consulting + lender database + done-for-you execution. Which were you picturing?" *Kills the broker-mismatch that once ended a 60-minute call at the close.*

**Step 12 — Bucket Discernment (prospect self-selects).** "Three buckets: 1) teach me, 2) do it for me, 3) hybrid — do it for me while teaching me so I can fund myself forever. Which fits you?" Assumptive variant: "Normally we teach this — but you're super busy, so that doesn't sound like you, correct?" *Kills "I could do this myself." Danger: bucket 1 + expert identity = Expert's Ego → pivot to unsell.*

**Step 13 — Timing, Logistics & Commitment.** "Why now vs later? Anything in the way — projects, vacations? Successful clients tie in 30–60 min/day — realistic for you?" ## PART IV — PITCH (5–10 min)

**Step 16 — Preface.** "The goal: $___ in funding. How we've done it — 500→$500K personally, $10M+ for clients — is a three-stage process." Slides: 1–2 per stage, bullets only; closer does the talking.

**Step 17 — Stage 1: Credit Optimization.** Callback→Solution→Benefit→Prompt. An uncured "7" becomes "I'll do research."

**Step 21 — Next Steps / Future Pace.** 10–15 seconds: "Agreement → payment → onboarding: easy videos, day-by-day." *Yes now has a picture.*

**Step 22 — Investment: Grand Slam Offer Assembly.** Order: **VALUE STACK → ROI → PRICE DROP → SILENCE.** Five components:
1. **Refundable deposit + funding guarantee** — "$2,000 upfront, refundable if $20K minimum isn't secured — a 10x return. Make sense?" (current calibration: $5K / $50K floor)
2. **Best case / worst case** — "Best: significant funding, the fee becomes irrelevant. Worst: full refund PLUS a written explanation of why. Either way you win."
3. **Transparency stack** — walk the whole tiered fee table aloud (6% first $100K → 1% above $1M; milestone-keyed success fees; "under $40K funded you pay nothing") — "and it's all in writing." Minor cons first, then pro-stack.
4. **Ask for MORE — never preemptively discount.** The $15K close came from asking higher. Ladder $8K→$6K→$4K→$2K exists only for live objections, backend rising as upfront falls.
5. **Micro-commitment floor** — $300 deposit keeps a money-tight deal alive.
Then: **silence.**

**Step 23 — Answer All + Assume the Sale.** "Ready to get started, or any questions?" → "Ready to get the ball rolling?" (never "Is anything stopping you?"). If Steps 1–22 ran, this is administrative.

**Step 24 — Objections: Isolate + Solve (4-category diagnostic: Uncertainty / Finances / Partner / Timing).** The elimination walk: "Makes sense? You understand it? You want the funding? Time's committed, partner's on board… so the only piece left is the fee itself." Call out the unspoken: "Prospects never say 'it's not worth it' to your face — 0% of the time — but they think it. Do you have the finances, and do you see the value?" "Think about it" → "Walk me through your thought process." Same answer twice → suggest the objection yourself and re-open that stage. Guarantee questions: "I can't control any institution's protocols. What I can say: we make your profile so underwriting-green-light compatible that it becomes very, very unreasonable not to succeed." **Every objection maps backward: Uncertainty→16–20 · Finances→7+22 · Partner→5 · Timing→13. An objection = a skipped step. Fix the step, not the symptom.**

**Step 25 — Safety, Personal Guarantee, Agreement LAST.** "My reputation is on the line. I only deserve your money if I deliver value." Guarantee = personal integrity, not a clause. Agreement presented last, after everything is resolved. (This exact cycle closed the $12K.)

**Step 26 — Pull-Back + Booked Next Step (never a dead end).** "The decision is yours — ball's in your court." ("Half a step before their guard comes up, pull back.") **No call ends without a calendared next step** — the winning model booked same-day 5:15 before hanging up.

---

## THE OBJECTION PRE-HANDLE MAP

| Objection | Killed at Step | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Price | 7, 8, 22 | Their ROI number vs fee; refundable guarantee; ask-more-then-ladder |
| Spouse / partner | 5 (+triage) | Reconfirm before discovery; buy-in via partners' goals |
| "Think about it" | 4, 20, 24, 26 | Yes/no contract; temp-check; elimination walk; booked follow-up |
| Broker expectation | 11 | Expectation check early |
| DIY ego | 10, 12, 17 | Their failed attempts; bucket self-selection; underwriting moat + unsell |
| Burned before | 3, 4, 15, 22, 25 | Metrics story; no-pressure frame; industry critique; in writing; personal guarantee |
| Competitor shopping | 22 | Motivation-drops-after-cap risk + uncapped continued-work guarantee |
| "Licensed?" | 3 | Track record vs paper ($10M+ funded) |
| Can't afford | 22.5 | Micro-deposit or $0-up/higher-backend for qualified profiles |

Four self-sells before any price: (1) motivation in their own words (2); (2) micro-agreement ladder — frame-yes, context-yes, permission-yes, per-stage yeses; (3) bucket self-selection (12); (4) temp-check 1–10 (20). 2. **The Preemptive Discount** — a $2K close that should have been more; price dropped before any objection existed. Countermove: open at top tier; descend only under live objection; the $15K close proves the market pays.
3. **The Open Loop** — offers without a booked next step die quietly. Countermove: calendar the follow-up before hanging up, every time; plant competitor counters before they compare; book the research-review call on the spot.

**Framework v2 — the Masterful Edition — is published: [MASTER CLOSING FRAMEWORK v2](https://app.notion.com/p/3b95bb1ffef481f293fbeaf311e224e4).** v1 now carries a supersession banner. Your instinct about the earlier version was validated in the hardest way: **the judge panel caught four invented "facts" in the draft** — a fabricated composite quote, a claimed live-booking that Jill actually declined on tape, an invented gate — all removed and replaced with what the tape really shows. That's the difference the adversarial pass bought.

What makes v2 a different class of document:

- **Doctrine vs. tape separated** — Constantine's fixed skeleton stands apart from the 28 compiled moves from your recordings, so nothing borrowed masquerades as doctrine. Two missing doctrine steps were restored (gap admission; alternatives-elimination + ROI-before-price).
- **Every quote is tiered**: tape-verified / summary-verbatim / NEEDS SOURCE — with a formal evidence ledger, verbatim hygiene (real stutters kept, six diarization-uncertain quotes flagged, a dozen timestamps corrected), and a **NEEDS WINNING TAPE registry of 12 honest gaps** instead of filler.
- **PART 0: the Current Offer Sheet** — prices, backend, guarantee, discount/concession menu, payment rails, all tape-sourced, with OWNER CONFIRM flags where only you can validate.
- **The two-call architecture** is now explicit: single-vs-two-call decision rule, the end-of-call-1 booking script, the 35-minute price law, and the two same-evening followow-up emails the earlier drafts missed.
- **Census truth**: "let me think about it" and affordability objections showed up on *wins* (Leo, Ashwini) and were converted — v2 teaches the conversion instead of pretending good calls never hear them.
- **The hard-mode material is in**: Matt's pricing-conflict → household-close mechanics, Leo's agreement-review trust repair, and the boundary lesson.
- **The quick-reference card was rebuilt** into three lanes (first call / close call / agreement review) with pacing marks and the sub-8 temp-check exit route.
- One factual bonus: Fathom metadata confirmed **Pradeep Bhatia (8/7) and P Reddy (8/10) are genuinely different prospects** — both records stand.

Your review targets: the **OWNER CONFIRM flags** in the Offer Sheet and the **12-item NEEDS WINNING TAPE registry** — those close from GHL call recordings and future tape, and the adjudication appendix records every judge fix the writer accepted or rejected with reasons.

> ⚠️ **PROCESS UPDATE — 2026-08-13. Two changes that override steps below.**
> Source: team calls [784176539](https://fathom.video/calls/784176539) and [784578211](https://fathom.video/calls/784578211).
>
> **1. Two dispute packages now exist — V2 is the DEFAULT.**
> - **V1 — Identity Theft Complaint.** The older path. Requires notarization and a police report, which is what makes it slow.
> - **V2 — Data Breach Statement.** *Now the default*, because it avoids the notarization and police-report delays. Uses a data-breach statement plus an FTC report.
> - **V2 mechanics:** file **one** FTC report, then modify and save it per bureau to produce **three distinct reports**, each tailored to that bureau's data.
> - **V2 still requires** a V2 Affidavit **and** a Limited Power of Attorney (LPOA) signed by the client — send the notarization form early, as this gates filing.
>
> **2. Experian disputes must use the DISPUTE CENTER report — not the standard consumer report.**
> This is not a preference. The Dispute Center report carries materially more data (30+ addresses vs. ~6 on the consumer report), which is what enables comprehensive removals. Pulling the wrong report silently limits what you can dispute.
>
> Everything below remains valid procedure; apply these two rules on top.

> ⚠️ **LIVE DIVERGENCE — the team changed the script on 2026-08-18/19. Reconcile before training anyone from this document.**
>
> **1. "What motivated you to reach out?" was REMOVED from the sales SOP.**
> Team rationale ([fathom.video/calls/789918031](https://fathom.video/calls/789918031)): *the question often invites clients to disqualify themselves and kills call momentum.*
> **This document teaches the opposite.** Step 2 treats that question as the first plank of the pre-sold mechanism — self-sold data harvested in the prospect's own words, later reused as callback ammunition. Both positions are defensible; what is not defensible is a closer being trained from two contradictory sources. **Alan to rule.** Until then, treat the SOP as operative for live calls and this step as under review.
>
> **2. "Any questions?" → "Was that helpful?"**
> Reason: the open-ended version invites deep technical tangents. This does *not* conflict with the framework's per-stage prompts, but the safer wording should replace "What questions do you have?" in Steps 17–19.
>
> **3. A two-step close is now the standard shape.**
> Call 1 (setter/Carla): qualify + pre-frame. Call 2: technical consultation with the funding specialist, **requiring the credit report**. The framework's two-call architecture section already models this — align the naming.
>
> **4. Pricing has moved again — three structures now exist in the wild.**
> New 3-tier strategy ([fathom.video/calls/790053322](https://fathom.video/calls/790053322)): **(1)** $0 upfront / 5–8% success fee for ready profiles · **(2)** an optimization fee for profile cleanup · **(3)** **PRIME Program, a $10k hybrid consulting model**. This does **not** match the $8K/$6K/$4K/$2K ladder in the Pricing SOP, nor the **$20K high-tier** quoted live to Yeshaya on 8/14. Part 0 of this document (Offer Sheet) is now stale. See the Master Ops Checklist pricing item.

addedBlocks:
## Nimble
Nimble turns the web into structured data. Use these product names exactly: Search, Answer, Extract, Extraction Template, Web Search Agent, Map, Crawl. Never call an Extraction Template a Web Search Agent (or vice versa).

Route by intent:

1. Named site + a direct item (URL or site-specific ID): nimble_extract_templates_list → get → run. Prefer a Nimble-maintained Extraction Template. If none matches, use a Web Search Agent — do not generate a new Extraction Template and do not dump a raw Extract.

2. Web Search Agent (nimble_agents_*): research, data enrichment, dataset building, named-subject information gathering, "extract all …" without a URL, catalog/directory entity lists, and any fan-out beyond 1–few already-known URLs. Reuse order: nimble_agents_list → nimble_agent_templates_list → create/run. Set use_case to research, enrichment, or dataset_building. Poll nimble_agents_run_status then nimble_agents_run_result. Gallery templates (nimble_agent_templates_*) are not Extraction Templates.

3. Search (nimble_search): only a single closed lookup — who/what at a glance, filing/page pointer, reverse lookup, named-channel presence. For a closed synthesized fact, set include_answer=true (Answer). Do not complete research or dataset asks with Search.

4. Extract (nimble_extract): one known URL, one-time. Check Extraction Templates first when the site is named. Not for "extract all", catalogs, or more than a few known URLs — that fan-out is a Web Search Agent.

5. Map (nimble_map): list the URLs on a site. Crawl (nimble_crawl_run): one-time bulk fetch of a known doc tree or URL list — not catalogs or entity sets.

Never invent live prices or news from training data. If a run is empty or wrong, say so and recover in the same capability (different param) before switching class. nimble_extract_templates_generate / update_from_template only when the user explicitly asks to create or refine a reusable Extraction Template — not as the no-template fallback.

**Big day. A two-week mystery solved, a major decision landing Tuesday, and one call I'd want you to look at personally.**

## ✅ "Coral" identified — it's Karl Krummenacher

The name was almost certainly mis-transcribed from audio. Every detail matches: **Modern Thyroid Clinic**, telemedicine, $8M revenue this year growing to $12–13M next, seeking the **$500–750K LOC**. Record renamed and filled in.

**And his decision is Tuesday.** He's comparing your **Prime -1% LOC with a 1% performance fee** against a competitor's **$350K at a higher rate but no origination fee**, deciding with his partner McCall at their executive meeting. Yours is larger and cheaper on rate — the competitor's only edge is the absent fee. **The entire decision is total cost of capital**, so a side-by-side interest-vs-fees comparison before Tuesday is the whole game. He's also targeting a $40–60M exit in 18–36 months, which makes him a relationship worth more than this one deal.

## ⚠️ Michael Moore — this one needs your judgment

New prospect needing $20–30K to finish a wellness center. His circumstances: **$10K cash, no income, recently left work after a cancer diagnosis**, and already enrolled in a JG Wentworth program that's advising him to **default on ~$75K** in card debt.

The strategy proposed on the call was a "utilization reset" — an **unfunded payment from a dummy account** timed before the statement close so near-zero utilization reports, producing a temporary 750–800 score to apply on. I logged it factually without endorsing it and flagged it for your decision, because two questions sit under it: whether applying on a score produced that way is a misrepresentation to the lender, and whether a client with no income in active debt relief is a fit for new credit at all. Worth deciding **before** an application goes in.

**Matt's dispute packets are finalized** for both Experian and TransUnion, and they used **V1, not V2** — which corrects the SOP banner I wrote last week. The real rule is item-dependent: **V2 for inquiries and minor items, V1 (with affidavit) for serious items like collections.** I've corrected the SOP, along with two new rules: every dispute must be submitted alongside its source credit report for side-by-side validation, and documents now live in Google Docs rather than edited PDFs, because version confusion was stalling filings for weeks.

## Your unit economics are now on the record

**16% show rate and $1,250 cost per qualified booked call** — targets are 60%+ and under $300. Against this tracker's own numbers (~$91–112 per *booking*), that gap is precisely the show-rate problem in dollars. Also noted: the new top-tier offer has been named **"Reserve,"** which may be the intended canonical answer to the four competing pricing structures.

**Leo has now missed four consecutive sweeps** — still $12,000 signed and uncollected.

Alan secured the deal: **$750K line of credit at WSJ Prime -1%**, with a **1% success fee = $7,500** to APW. The pricing rationale is worth keeping for the playbook — the 1% was set deliberately to match what a prior broker had charged him, so the number felt native rather than negotiated. **I held him at Offer Made, not Closed Won** — no contract is signed yet, and the next action is specific: the contract must be simple and **"red-flag-free"** because it goes to a high-net-worth entrepreneur's legal team, where anything aggressive stalls it.

> 🔑 **THE TRANSUNION "ONE DISPUTE" WORKAROUND — added 2026-08-24.** Source: [fathom.video/calls/796461872](https://fathom.video/calls/796461872). This solves the blocker that stalled Todd's and Matt's files for weeks.
>
> **The problem:** TransUnion's portal **freezes during an active dispute**. While one dispute is open, no new submission can be made — which is why files sat stuck rather than progressing.
>
> **The workaround, in order:**
> 1. **File a CFPB complaint FIRST.** This creates a documented, timestamped record that the 605B packet was sent — independent of TU's frozen portal.
> 2. **Call TransUnion** and confirm receipt of the CFPB-filed documents.
> 3. **Immediately request transfer to "Special Handlings" or "Identity Theft."** Do not attempt to work the item with a generalist agent — these departments hold the authority to process rapid removals. Requesting the department by name is what gets you there.
>
> **FTC report leverage (use when the client already has one):** an FTC identity-theft report **does not expire**, and there is a **lifetime limit of 5 reports**. Stating both makes "just file a new report" an unreasonable ask, and in practice it prompts immediate action instead of a deferral.
>
> Combine with the standing rule below: every dispute document must match the **Experian Dispute Center report** (not the consumer report), and V1 (affidavit) is for serious items like collections while V2 is for inquiries and minor items.

**Monday's restart — five recordings, all internal, but two of them mattered.**

## 🔑 The TransUnion blocker was cracked

This is the most useful thing to come out of the week. **TransUnion's portal freezes during an active dispute** — which is precisely why Todd's and Matt's files sat stuck. The workaround discovered today, now written into the Bureau Call Script SOP:

1. **File a CFPB complaint first** — creates a timestamped record that the 605B packet was sent, independent of the frozen portal
2. **Call TU** and confirm receipt of the CFPB-filed documents
3. **Immediately request "Special Handlings" or "Identity Theft"** — asking for the department by name bypasses generalist agents who can't process rapid removals

Plus a leverage point worth remembering: an FTC identity-theft report **doesn't expire** and there's a **lifetime limit of 5** — stating both makes "just file a new one" an unreasonable ask and tends to prompt immediate action.

## Client progress on two files

**Todd's account is "nearly complete"** — the three-bureau deadlock appears broken, almost certainly by that workaround. **Two accounts eliminated for Ed C.** One thing to confirm: whether those two are the Hancock Whitney pair Experian refused to fraud-block on 8/14, because if so, the forced 30-day route delivered ahead of its ~Sep 11 window.

A **one-week trial period is now in effect for the entire team — including Alan** — weighted 80% results, 15% character, 5% punctuality, with termination for missing standards. Structure changes: the daily meeting splits into a 30-min huddle plus mandatory department meetings (including a new 8am dispute-team session), SODRs move to Trello checklists, Notion stays the client-documentation system.

Karl (no activity since 8/20 — worth watching for drift on a $7,500 deal awaiting only a contract), Leo, Zacherly, Michael M., Pedro, Connor, Stefan, Yeshaya, Jesse H., and the six never-dialed leads.

Terms agreed 8/20 on a $750K LOC worth $7,500 to APW, and nothing since. That's the largest live deal drifting on a single document.
